post.description:
One allocation by service id. Readable by any authenticated user in any state —
 an investor holding units of a closed product still needs to render it — but a
 product whose effective level for the caller is `hidden` is NOT_FOUND, the same
 answer an unregistered slug gets, so the catalog cannot be probed for locked
 products. An `AllocationManage` holder reads any allocation.

Raise one investor above the default (AllocationManage): `view` | `invest`. A
 repeat grant for the same user overwrites the level. A grant can only ever add —
 an investor's effective level is the higher of the default and the grant — so
 `hidden` is not a level a grant can carry; use Revoke to take one back.

post.summary:
Mint units to a holder with no cash leg (AllocationManage). The allocation must be
 registered, in any state — a product is normally seeded before it opens. The mint
 is priced at the current (fresh) NAV for the record and the holder's cost basis,
 and counts against the unit cap exactly as a subscription does: an operator sizing
 a product below what they mean to issue raises the cap first, then issues.
post.description:
Idempotent by `idempotency_key`, unique per service: a retry of a timed-out call
 returns the issuance the key already names and mints nothing. A key reused for a
 DIFFERENT holder or amount is ALREADY_EXISTS — the retry is the case the key exists
 for, the reuse is the mistake it has to catch.
Every standing grant on one allocation (AllocationManage), ordered by `user_id`.

The catalog. Any authenticated user sees the `open` allocations they may at least
 view; an `AllocationManage` holder may set `include_unlisted` to see drafts,
 closed and hidden ones too. Ordered by `service`.

The cap table of one product (AllocationManage): the settled supply and every
 holder of it — people, and the reserved `fee` allocation holding the product's fee
 class — largest first. Read straight from the ledger — the number an operator
 checks against the registration before opening a product to the market.

Register a new allocation in `draft` (AllocationManage). The service id is a
 1..64 char `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` slug and is immutable once registered; re-registering
 an existing one is a conflict, never a silent update.

post.summary:
Burn a holder's units with no cash leg (AllocationManage) — the reverse of
 IssueUnits: `units` leave the holder's account and the supply shrinks by the same
 amount. Nothing is paid; this is a cap-table correction,
 the way an in-kind mint was. The holder must have at least `units` AVAILABLE
 (Read-First; units resting on the book or reserved by a redemption do not count) —
 otherwise INVALID_ARGUMENT — and the allocation must be `closed`, because burning a
 holder's units out of a live product is a decision that deserves a closed door
 first; `force` is the explicit override for a live product (FAILED_PRECONDITION
 without it). Priced at the current (fresh) NAV for the record; the default
 `cost_basis` is `units × NAV`, the book value written off.
post.description:
Answers a `UnitIssuance` with `source = "retire"` and POSITIVE `units`: the row is
 the magnitude, the source is the direction, and the console lists mints and
 retirements as one history. Idempotent by `idempotency_key` in the same key space
 as IssueUnits: the same key naming a mint and then a retirement is ALREADY_EXISTS,
 not a retry.

Take a per-user grant back (AllocationManage). Idempotent — revoking a grant that
 does not exist succeeds and changes nothing. The investor falls back to the
 default level; units they already hold are unaffected and still redeemable.

Set the default access level (AllocationManage): `hidden` | `view` | `invest`.
 Idempotent. Separate from SetAllocationState because the two answer different
 questions — `state` is whether the product deals, `access` is who it deals with —
 and collapsing them would make "open but invite-only" unexpressible. Lowering
 the default never touches a per-user grant, and never touches redemptions.

Declare what stands behind a product's units (AllocationManage): `cash` |
 `in_kind`. Idempotent. `in_kind` is set automatically by the first `IssueUnits`,
 never the reverse: this RPC is how an operator says the fund now holds cash for
 the units and `Redeem` may pay it out again — or corrects a product back to
 `in_kind`. Lifecycle, access and holdings are untouched.

Drive the lifecycle (AllocationManage): `open` or `close`. Idempotent — setting
 the state an allocation already holds succeeds and changes nothing.

Resize the authorised unit supply (AllocationManage). Idempotent. Separate from
 UpdateAllocation because this one gates money: `Subscribe` refuses a mint that
 would carry the issued supply past the cap. A cap below what is already issued is
 legal and means "no more units" — nothing minted is affected and redemptions are
 untouched, so this can never strand a holder. Zero is refused: use
 SetAllocationState(`closed`) to stop new money, which says so in the state.

Update the presentation fields of an existing allocation (AllocationManage).
 Never changes state or identity.

Mint the money-plane token pair for an already-identified user, keyed by their
 concierge user id. Service-to-service: authenticated by the shared issuance token
 in the `authorization` metadata (Bearer), never a user token. The user must already
 exist locally (provisioned by the cross-plane bridge) and not be frozen.

Publish the current signing public keys (JWKS). Polled by downstream services'
 `evbanking_auth` verifier to refresh its local cache; also consulted on an
 unknown-`kid` miss. Carries only public key material.

List the caller's active sessions (refresh-token families). Identity is proven by
 the presented refresh token (the BFF holds it server-side); the family that owns
 that token is flagged `current`.

Revoke the presented refresh token's family. With `revoke_all` set, also bumps
 the user's `token_version` so every outstanding access token is rejected hub-side.

Rotate a refresh token: returns a fresh access+refresh pair and invalidates
 the presented refresh token (rotation + reuse detection in the central store).

Revoke one of the caller's sessions by id (must belong to the same user). Revoking
 the current session is allowed (acts like a sign-out of this device).

Dispatch a queued withdrawal to custody once its rail has liquidity (the treasury
 worker). Stands in for an automated rebalance/top-up trigger. Idempotent.

Fail a queued fund redemption (operator): voids the reserved burn, returning the
 user's units. Idempotent.

Fail a processing user withdrawal that never reached the chain: voids the
 reservation, refunding the user. NEVER call this if the broadcast may have landed
 on-chain — that would double-pay. Idempotent.

What the platform has EARNED: the `fee` allocation, in the same shape the treasury
 lists every allocation in — its cash (settled / reserved / available), its supply,
 its price and who holds it. Admin/Owner. Nothing pays it out from here: a holder is
 paid by redeeming their units, and a payment out of its claim is an order the owners
 approve (`PaymentsService.OpenPayment` with source `{kind: "service", id: "fee"}`).
 `banking_treasury` is banking's own treasury beside it (D17); nothing pays out of it
 until concierge's scope approvals decide its spending (D24).
Operator (TreasuryRead): the money-plane operations mode (the read-only kill-switch).

The treasury: per-rail on-chain liquidity (Layer 2) and the claims it backs
 (Layer 1), read live from TigerBeetle (Read-First).
Operator (TreasuryRead): outbox rows the relay parked (needs-intervention).

Operator (TreasuryRead): every rail, whether this deployment runs it, and whether an
 operator froze it.

Operator (RedemptionSettle): the cross-user queue of redemptions awaiting settle,
 oldest first — the "Valuation & redemptions" screen's clear-the-queue surface.
 (Est. cash = units × current NAV is computed client-side from the posted NAV.)

Admin (WithdrawalSettle): the cross-user queue of withdrawals awaiting operator
 action, oldest first — `queued` (awaiting liquidity/dispatch) and `processing`
 (broadcast in flight: settle with the mined tx ref, or fail ONLY if nothing
 reached the chain). The admin Withdrawals screen's clear-the-queue surface.

post.summary:
Admin (DepositAddressMigrate): retire a user's HEALTHY, KEK-sealed deposit address
 in favour of one minted inside the key custodian's enclave (phase 4 of
 docs/MIGRATION-turnkey.md), and refresh the hub's address cache.
post.description:
NOT the rotation path. Rotation recovers a key that is already dead; this retires a
 live one, so the hub must first prove the address has nothing left on it — refused
 while the user has any credited deposit on this rail that no sweep has observed
 drained. The signer independently refuses a dead key, an already-migrated row, and
 an address other than the one this hub cleared.

Post a fund's total AUM; NAV is derived = AUM / units_outstanding (units read live
 from TigerBeetle). Rejects zero units and a NAV move beyond the safety threshold —
 measured against BOTH the previous mark and the mark that anchored the rolling
 window, so the cap cannot be walked past in steps. There is NO per-request override:
 a move past the cap is put to the owners through
 `ConsiliumService.OpenValuationOverride`, and only an executed consilium records it.

Record a settled on-chain deposit, crediting a party's claim. Idempotent by
 `tx_ref` — recording the same chain tx twice credits once.

Admin (DepositAddressRotate): supersede a user's PROVABLY DEAD deposit address
 (the signer can no longer unseal its key — the KEK-epoch casualty class) with a
 freshly minted keypair, and refresh the hub's address cache. The signer refuses
 to rotate a key that still unseals. Funds already on the old address remain
 unrecoverable; this restores the user's ability to receive FUTURE deposits.

Propose a seed of the platform's capital: a transfer that reached a rail's treasury
 address from outside, PROVEN against the chain, to be booked as the depositor's
 deposit and subscribed into the `fund` allocation — units of `fund` for the person
 whose money it was. This OPENS A CONSILIUM and books nothing: the chain proves the
 dollar arrived, it cannot say whose it is, and the first administrator to name a
 reference must not be the one who decides. The caller must hold an owner seat. The
 arrival is verified now (same verification as RecordDeposit, against
 `expected_amount`); a transfer to a user's deposit address is that user's deposit
 and is refused (record it with RecordDeposit); the sweep is refused; a reference
 already recorded is a conflict.

Admin (OperationsManage): toggle read-only mode. When on, every user money mutation
 (withdraw / subscribe / redeem) is rejected — "pause deposits & withdrawals".

Admin (OperationsManage): freeze/unfreeze a rail — no new deposit addresses or
 withdrawals on it, queued withdrawals held, and no treasury gas alert.

Settle a queued fund redemption once the fund's claim is liquid (the treasury
 worker): prices at the settle-time NAV and pays the cash. Idempotent.

Settle a user withdrawal once it has the required on-chain confirmations: posts the
 reservation and moves the net out of custody. `tx_ref` is the chain transaction.
 Stands in for a chain watcher + custody confirmation callback. Idempotent.

Admin (OutboxManage): clear `parked_at` so the relay re-drives the event once the
 cause is fixed; refused for a compensated row — it parked half-applied with
 compensation owed, so re-driving would re-apply the legs that already posted.

Take the caller's resting order off the book; its unspent escrow is released.
 Idempotent on an already-cancelled order; a filled one is ALREADY_EXISTS.

The aggregated book: the top `depth` price levels a side, the last trade, the
 24h figures, and the fund's NAV for the ticker. Readable by anyone who may view the
 allocation; a hidden one is NOT_FOUND, as on AllocationsService.
The allocation's trading terms. Readable by anyone who may view the allocation.

OHLCV candles aggregated from the tape over `[from, to)`, one per non-empty bucket
 at `resolution` (1m | 5m | 15m | 1h | 4h | 1d). Buckets with no trade are omitted —
 a chart carries the last close forward itself.

The caller's resting orders (`open` | `partially_filled`), oldest first, optionally
 on one allocation.
The caller's orders in every state, newest first, optionally on one allocation.

The public tape, newest first: price, size, the taker's side and the time. No
 order ids and no parties — a counterparty is never disclosed.

The caller's own fills, newest first: each carries the caller's side, their order
 id and the fee they paid on it.

post.summary:
Place an order for the caller. Limit orders carry a `price` on the policy's tick;
 market orders leave it empty and are priced by the hub from the best opposite quote
 ± the policy's slippage, then run as an IOC limit at that price (an empty opposite
 side is FAILED_PRECONDITION). `size` is on the policy's lot.
post.description:
Refusals: `book_open = false`, or the caller below `invest` — FAILED_PRECONDITION;
 a post-only (`alo`) order that would cross, or one that would trade against the
 caller's own resting order — INVALID_ARGUMENT, nothing recorded; an insufficient
 available balance or holding — INVALID_ARGUMENT.

 Idempotent by `client_order_id`, unique per caller: a retry of a timed-out call
 returns the order the id already names. The same id for a DIFFERENT order is
 ALREADY_EXISTS.

Replace the allocation's trading terms (AllocationManage). Closing the book
 (`book_open = false`) stops new orders; resting ones stay and may still be cancelled.

The caller's balance in ONE scope (`main` included), for a client that shows a single
 compartment and must not read the sum over all of them. An unknown scope is NOT_FOUND.

A scope service's stored request for a mandate (`scope.v1.MandateRequestService`),
 for the caller to read before granting it. Unknown, expired and malformed ids are
 the same NOT_FOUND; the id is a lowercase uuid.

One scope's policy, read-only. The platform owners set it (an approval of kind
 `bank:compartment_policy`), never the user.

Let a scope's service draw on the caller's compartment in that scope — hold it
 (a subscription, a buy order) or charge it — within the caps of the service's
 request, which the caller grants as it stands (`request_id`; unknown or expired is
 NOT_FOUND). This is
 the only consent a service's debit stands on; without it the service can only
 send an invoice. A client that banking's grants do not allow to touch users'
 compartments in the scope is INVALID_ARGUMENT. One live mandate per (scope,
 client): granting again replaces it — new holds and charges draw on the new one,
 while holds already standing stay under the mandate they were placed with until they
 finish. The new mandate still binds them: none outlives its `expires_at`, and a
 capture of one into another user needs BOOK_FILL from both. Naturally confirmed on
 the caller's first move into the scope, on one screen.

Every scope the caller could hold money in: `main` first, then each scope banking
 knows, with the caller's balance there (zero if never entered) and its policy.

The caller's live mandates, and replaced ones whose holds still hold money, newest
 first.

Move money between `main` and one scope compartment — exactly one side is `main`.
 Moving IN is checked against the scope's policy: FAILED_PRECONDITION with the
 failed rule (`kyc_level`, `max_per_move`, `max_moved_in_24h`, `max_balance`) when
 it does not pass. Moving OUT is never limited by policy, only by what is available
 in the compartment. Either way `insufficient_funds` when the source, less the
 caller's moves still in flight, cannot cover it; the limits count moves in flight too.
 A key reused with different terms is ALREADY_EXISTS. The move is recorded at once and
 posted to the ledger by the hub: the result's `state` is `pending` until then,
 `posted` after, or `failed` (with `failure_reason`) if the ledger refused it or the
 hub could not post it — a failed move is final and is never carried out later.

End a live mandate at once. Every hold the client still has on the caller's
 compartment in the scope is voided — under this mandate or one it replaced — so the
 money is back with the caller, and the service learns it from the money events. A
 mandate already revoked or replaced is returned as it is; anyone else's, or an
 unknown id, is NOT_FOUND.

The redacted invitation behind an emailed token. Side-effect free. Unknown,
 expired, spent and wrong-state tokens all return the SAME NOT_FOUND, so this
 cannot be used to probe which is which.

Cast this owner's vote. Requires the token AND the secret code from the mail.
 Five failed code attempts burn the token permanently.
Withdraw an invoice the caller opened, while it is still OPEN.
One consilium in full, including per-voter state (Owner only).
Consilia newest first — the governance history (Owner only).

Seat a new holder of a reserved allocation (Owner only): `units` of `fee` or `fund`
 minted to a person, with no cash leg, once the quorum carries. The units are
 frozen into the terms, not a cash figure — what they are worth is the allocation's
 NAV at execution, as a subscription is priced at its own moment. Refused when the
 person is not an active user, when the allocation is not reserved, or when the
 roster is too small. This is the ONLY way a person comes to hold `fee` or `fund`
 other than a seed (`BalanceService.SeedCapital`) or the book.

Put a NAV mark the move guard refuses to the owners (ValuationPost holders — the
 poster proposes, the owners decide). Executing it records the mark at exactly this
 AUM, guard or no guard; there is no other way past the guard. One open request per
 fund: it shares the fund's `service:<id>` claim with a payment out of that claim.

Take responsibility for the holders of a scheduled change who could not be told
 (AllocationManage, AND the caller must be the one who requested the change or a fund
 owner). A change that TIGHTENS the terms does not bind while a holder's notice is
 undelivered; for a holder the identity plane can never reach that is forever. This
 records who acknowledged, when, and exactly which holders' notices the mailer had
 GIVEN UP on by that moment (`notices_given_up`, never a notice still being tried), and
 the change then binds over those holders — and over nobody else who turns out untold
 later. A later call ADDS the holders given up on since (`notices_unacknowledged`) and
 stands as the latest: its caller and moment replace the record's, taking
 responsibility for the whole list. A repeat that would add nobody returns the record
 unchanged. ALREADY_EXISTS when the change is not scheduled, only loosens the terms (it
 binds by itself), or has no notice given up on yet that is not already covered —
 there is nothing to take responsibility for; PERMISSION_DENIED for a caller who is
 neither the requester nor an owner.

Withdraw a pending change (AllocationManage). One still awaiting the owners takes its
 consilium down with it. Idempotent on an already-cancelled change.

What the caller's holding owes right now WITHOUT charging it: the management fee
 accrued since the last charge, the performance fee that would crystallize at
 today's NAV, and any carried debt. This is what a position's "value net of fees"
 must subtract, and it carries the investor's own mark so the figure is explicable.

One fund's terms, or an empty policy when the product charges nothing. Readable
 by any authenticated user — an investor is entitled to know what they are paying.

The fund's accumulated, unconverted fee units and what they are worth
 (AllocationManage).

The caller's own fee statement, newest first — every charge, what it was for, and
 anything that deferred.
Every configured policy, ordered by service. Readable by any authenticated user.

A fund's whole history of terms, newest version first. Readable by any
 authenticated user — the terms one is on, and how they came to be, are public
 information about a product.
Every charge against one fund (AllocationManage).

post.summary:
Propose a change of a fund's terms (AllocationManage — the same trust seam as
 bringing the product into existence or posting its valuation). The service must
 already be a registered allocation. Rates are basis points, capped at 500
 (management, 5% p.a.) and 5000 (performance, 50% of the gain); the hurdle at 10000.
post.description:
A policy is never edited in place. The change is recorded with a version and takes
 effect no earlier than 24h after it was scheduled while anyone holds units (at once
 for a fund with no holders); `effective_from` may ask for later, never earlier. A
 change that TIGHTENS the terms beyond the house envelope (2-and-20 on invested
 capital, annual) needs the owners' consilium, which the caller must be an owner to
 open, and `reason` is then required; every other change is scheduled at once. The
 holders are mailed when the change is scheduled. One pending change per fund: a
 second is refused with ALREADY_EXISTS until the first is cancelled.

Convert accumulated fee units into the `fee` allocation's cash (AllocationManage).
 Omit `units` to settle the whole balance. Refused — never queued — when the fund's
 claim cannot cover the payout: nobody is waiting on this, and unconverted fee units
 keep accumulating at no cost. The settler is the CALLER, never a field: whoever
 posted the product's latest mark cannot settle its fee class for 7 days, so a
 request cannot name somebody else to get past that.
Cancel a still-queued redemption (returns the reserved units).
The current NAV (price per share) for a fund, plus freshness.
The caller's position in one fund (units, NAV, value, cost basis, P&L).

The posted valuation marks of one allocation over a window, plus the caller's own
 participation (units held × NAV) through it — the two series of the performance chart.
All of the caller's fund positions.
The caller's redemptions for the fund surface (newest first).
Redeem `units` of a fund back to cash (accept-and-queue; settle-time priced).

Subscribe `amount` of free balance into a fund, minting units at the current NAV.
 Returns the mint receipt; the holding updates once the relay applies it.

The invoice as the payer sees it. Unknown ids and invoices restricted to another
 payer are the SAME NOT_FOUND.

Pay an OPEN invoice. FAILED_PRECONDITION when it is no longer open, when the
 chosen source cannot cover it, or when the payer is below the receiving scope's
 `min_kyc_level`. A repeat with the same `idempotency_key` returns
 the invoice you paid; paying it again under a new key is FAILED_PRECONDITION.
 PAID MEANS POSTED. The answer is the invoice as it stands now: `processing` while the
 ledger has not taken the payment (normally milliseconds), `paid` once it has. A
 payment the ledger refuses puts the invoice back to `open`, payable again. Poll
 `GetPayableInvoice` until it leaves `processing`.
The caller's operations, newest first, across all four kinds.

Answer: APPROVE or REJECT. Idempotent for the same answer; a different one after an
 answer is ALREADY_EXISTS. An approval is gated like any money the caller moves (revoked
 tokens, the operator's pause, a frozen account) and executed at once; a failure in the
 execution is the order's to record and does not undo the answer. A seat whose pins have
 moved (the caller's sessions were revoked, or their mailbox changed, since the order
 opened) fails the order closed and answers ALREADY_EXISTS with the reason.
One order as its subject may see it, whatever state it is in.
The caller's orders waiting for their answer, newest first.

The redacted invitation behind an emailed token. Side-effect free. Unknown, expired,
 spent, burned and closed tokens all return the SAME NOT_FOUND.

Answer the consent. Requires the token AND the secret code from the mail. Five failed
 code attempts burn the token permanently — and, with one seat, fail the payment closed.
Withdraw an order the CALLER opened, while it is still pending. Anyone else is refused.
One order in full (Admin/Owner).
The payment history, newest first, filtered (Admin/Owner). Nothing is ever deleted.

Open a payment order (Admin/Owner). Refused when the source cannot cover the amount
 right now, when the shape could never execute (an unconfigured rail, a sub-minimum
 external amount, an external destination out of a service claim, the treasury as a
 destination), when the source is the treasury (closed, D24), or when another order is
 already open against the same service claim.

The id of the concierge approval opened for a payout operation, so the BFF can ask
 concierge whether the caller is on its roster BEFORE any recipient is read. Carries no
 line, no amount and no name.

One page of the operation's lines, with the summary every page repeats. `approval_id`
 must be the operation's own (from GetPayoutApproval).

Admin (allowlist): disable a user, freezing future sign-in/refresh without
 deleting the record.

The calling user's live balance — `main` plus their scope compartments — read straight
 from TigerBeetle (Read-First).
 No Postgres-stored amount exists; the response is authoritative as of `as_of`.
The calling user's own identity (resolved from the access-token `sub`).

Admin (UserBalanceRead): read ANY user's live balance by id — the operator
 console's user-detail drawer. The self-service GetBalance above acts on the
 caller's own `sub`; this one takes an explicit target and is role-gated.

Admin (allowlist): bump a user's token_version so all their outstanding access
 tokens are rejected hub-side. The token-revocation control surface.

Update the caller's own editable profile fields (full-replace of the set in
 UpdateProfileRequest). Identity/auth fields (email, status) are not editable here.

Cancel one of the caller's still-queued withdrawals (refund). Rejected once the
 withdrawal is processing (a broadcast may have landed).
The caller's deposit address on a network (stable; derived once and reused).

The caller's wallet — the unified lifecycle balance, deposit addresses, and the
 per-rail withdrawable view.
The caller's confirmed on-chain deposits, newest first.
The caller's withdrawals, newest first.

Request an on-chain withdrawal of free balance to an external address. Accepted
 (and reserved) as long as the unified balance covers it; it ships immediately when
 the chosen rail is liquid, otherwise it is queued until the treasury tops it up.

post.summary:
Redeem a one-time authorization code for a RELYING PARTY's own token pair — the
 back half of the code flow a first-party client on another origin (the Service-Arb
 panel) runs against `GET /auth/authorize` (publicly `evinvest.ltd/api/auth/authorize`).
 Called server-to-server by the client's backend, authenticated by its client
 secret. The code is single-use, lives 60s, and is bound to the client, the exact
 redirect_uri and the PKCE (S256) challenge sent to authorize; presenting a code
 twice is refused AND revokes every token issued off it.
post.description:
The access token is `typ=access` with `aud=<the client's audience>` (e.g. `sa`) and
 a TTL of at most 15 minutes. It opens exactly one RPC in this plane —
 `UserDirectory.GetMe`, which answers it with a trimmed profile (no identity-document
 fields, no KYC level) — and is refused (UNAUTHENTICATED) everywhere else, here and
 on the money plane. Signing out of evinvest.ltd (Logout, RevokeSession, revoke-all)
 revokes the client sessions that sign-in authorized. The refresh token is opaque and bound to the client.

Publish the current signing public keys (JWKS). Polled by downstream services'
 `evconcierge_auth` verifier to refresh its local cache; also consulted on an
 unknown-`kid` miss. Carries only public key material.

List the caller's active sessions (refresh-token families). Identity is proven by
 the presented refresh token (the BFF holds it server-side); the family that owns
 that token is flagged `current`.

Revoke the presented refresh token's family. With `revoke_all` set, also bumps
 the user's `token_version` so every outstanding access token is rejected.

A relying party publishes its tenant's catalog: the permissions and aliases its
 namespace defines. Authenticated by the client secret, like ExchangeCode. Refused
 (INVALID_ARGUMENT) when anything lies outside the tenant's namespace, an alias names
 a permission the catalog does not define, a delegated alias delegates in turn, the
 catalog exceeds 1024 permissions or 128 aliases or a name exceeds 128 characters, or
 `version` lies more than a day ahead of this plane's clock; FAILED_PRECONDITION when
 `version` is older than the stored one, or equal with different content. Every
 published catalog is kept. Grants whose target the new catalog drops stay, grant
 nothing, and are listed as orphaned.

Rotate a refresh token: returns a fresh access+refresh pair and invalidates
 the presented refresh token (rotation + reuse detection in the central store).

Rotate a relying party's refresh token. The account is re-checked on EVERY rotation,
 so a suspension ends the session at the next refresh rather than at the family's
 deadline; presenting a rotated-out token revokes the family.

Revoke one of the caller's sessions by id (must belong to the same user). Revoking
 the current session is allowed (acts like a sign-out of this device).
Withdraw an admission the caller opened, while it is still OPEN.
Withdraw a proposal the caller opened, while it is still OPEN.
Withdraw a user proposal the caller opened, while it is still OPEN.

Drain the window (reorganisation, expand step): void the OPEN legacy proposals named in
 the request, so this service's part of the consilia can be emptied before they move to
 ApprovalService. An owner only. Works whether or not new openings are closed
 (GOVERNANCE_NEW_VOTES_CLOSED). A proposal that is not open is reported, not changed.
The current owner roster (Owner only).

post.summary:
Propose granting Role::Admin (Owner only). UserDirectory.SetRole refuses that role
 in the granting direction and names this, for the same reason it already refuses
 `owner`: an operator who can appoint operators can appoint accomplices, and the
 admin seat carries every identity mutation except role granting.
post.description:
Taking the role away is NOT here and stays one act on purpose — containing a rogue
 operator must never be the slower path.

post.summary:
Propose GRANTING a seat (Owner only). The candidate does not vote — they are not
 yet an owner — and neither does the initiator, so the voters are every OTHER
 current owner and all of them must agree. A lone owner cannot open one at all.
post.description:
This is the only way `Role::Owner` is granted: UserDirectory.SetRole refuses it
 outside an executed admission.

Propose removing an owner (Owner only). The initiator casts no vote — proposing is
 not agreeing, and counting it would let two owners remove a third.

post.summary:
Propose lifting a suspension THE OWNERS imposed (Owner only). It exists because
 UserDirectory.ReinstateUser refuses those: without this RPC the consilium's verdict
 would be either permanent or reversible by any one admin, and both are wrong.
post.description: A hold needs nothing from here — ReinstateUser lifts one in a single act.

post.summary:
Propose PERMANENTLY suspending a user (Owner only). The half of the old
 DisableUser verb that is not an emergency: UserDirectory.HoldUser freezes the
 account now and lapses in 24h, and this is what makes it stay.
post.description:
A reason is required. It is what the other owners are voting on, and a decision to
 freeze somebody's account with no stated cause cannot be reviewed afterwards.

Resign your own seat. No consilium — but the same floor applies, so the last two
 owners cannot leave the fund without governance.

A peer owner's vote on an admission, cast in the cabinet while signed in. One
 REJECT ends it: admission passes only on unanimity.

A peer owner's vote, cast in the cabinet while signed in — this is the live
 consilium, not an emailed link. The target and the initiator are both refused.

An owner's vote on a user proposal. Unlike the OWNER consilia this passes on a
 MAJORITY of the snapshotted voters rather than unanimity — see UserProposal.

Enqueue one governance mail. Idempotent by `dedupe_key`, so an at-least-once
 caller may retry without sending twice.

The redacted invitation behind an emailed token. Unknown, expired, spent and
 wrong-state tokens all return the same NOT_FOUND.

The target accepting — or refusing — their own removal. Five failed code attempts
 burn the token permanently.

post.summary:
DEPRECATED — always refuses, naming HoldUser or
 ApprovalService.ProposeUserSuspension.
post.description:
The verb was ambiguous in the one way that mattered: it was both the emergency
 brake (the frozen flag the money plane re-reads at dispatch, which stops a
 withdrawal already in the queue) and a permanent judgement on an account, decided
 by one person with no record of why. Those need opposite treatments — the first
 must stay instant, the second must not be one person's to make — so the caller now
 has to say which one they mean. Kept in the contract rather than deleted so an
 older console gets an explanatory refusal instead of an UNIMPLEMENTED.
The calling user's own identity (resolved from the access-token `sub`).

Admin (UserRead): the full profile of ANY user by id (the admin sibling of the
 self-only GetMe), for the user-detail drawer.

post.summary:
Grant a user a target inside a tenant's namespace: an alias (`sa:operator`), a
 permission (`sa:work:leads:read`) or a `*` pattern (`sa:work:*`). Nothing grants
 anything in the `iam`, `concierge`, `bank` or `seat` namespaces (INVALID_ARGUMENT),
 and nobody grants to their own account (PERMISSION_DENIED). A target the tenant's
 catalog does not define grants nothing and is INVALID_ARGUMENT. Re-granting what is
 held is a no-op.
post.description:
Who may: a seat holding `iam:tenants:grant` — any target. The holder of an alias the
 catalog lets delegate (`delegations`) — exactly the aliases it delegates, naming the
 user by `account` (an email or a username) only (a `user_id` is PERMISSION_DENIED:
 ids are visible in the roster, and granting one would reveal its owner's address).
 Anyone else, or a target outside the delegation: PERMISSION_DENIED, before the user
 is looked up. An email names the accounts it is verified on or backs a password of;
 only when it names none is the handle read as a username.

 To a seat: an unknown user or handle is NOT_FOUND; a handle naming several
 accounts, or a disabled/held account, is FAILED_PRECONDITION with the reason. To a
 delegate all three are the SAME FAILED_PRECONDITION ("this address cannot be granted
 access"), so a grant never tells them whether, or how, a handle is known. A
 delegate gets a budget of GrantPermission + RevokePermission calls per hour
 (refusals included); past it, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED.

Admin (UserSuspend): the emergency brake. Freezes the account NOW and lapses on
 its own after 24h unless the owners ratify it with ProposeUserSuspension. One actor
 may stop money temporarily; one actor may never stop it permanently. Emits
 SUSPENDED across the cross-plane bridge, and REINSTATED again when it lapses.

The active grants inside one tenant namespace, with each holder's identity. A seat
 holding `iam:tenants:grant`, or a delegate of that namespace — who gets `legal_name`
 AND `preferred_name` empty: the team sees each other's email, username and grant, and
 nothing that says who an address belongs to.

Admin (UserRead): list/search users for the operator console — paginated, with a
 free-text query and optional role/status filters (see ListUsersRequest). Returns
 lightweight summaries, not full profiles.

post.summary:
Admin (allowlist): re-enable a disabled user, lifting the sign-in/refresh
 freeze. Emits REINSTATED across the cross-plane bridge.
post.description:
Refuses with FAILED_PRECONDITION when the suspension was the owners' verdict,
 naming ApprovalService.ProposeUserReinstatement — otherwise one admin could
 overturn a consilium and the consilium would be advisory.

Take a grant away. Same authority as GrantPermission, either addressing form for a
 delegate too: the answer depends only on a grant they can already list. NOT_FOUND when
 the user holds no active grant of that target — including a handle naming nobody, or
 several accounts. Shares GrantPermission's budget.

Admin (allowlist): bump a user's token_version so all their outstanding access
 tokens are rejected. The token-revocation control surface.

post.summary:
Admin (allowlist): set a user's KYC level. Emits KYC_CHANGED across the
 cross-plane bridge (so the money plane learns the new level). Echoes the
 level now in effect.
post.description:
Refuses with PERMISSION_DENIED when user_id is the CALLER's own account.
 KycManage is held by Admin as well as Owner, and tier 1 is the floor for
 withdrawals on the money plane, so without this an operator could lift their
 own money gate. A console must not offer this control on the operator's own
 row: the refusal is decided from the session alone and belongs in front of
 the call. Raising your own level goes through the verification front door,
 which reaches tier 1; above that, and for any downgrade, another holder of
 KycManage acts.

Admin (RoleGrant, Owner only): set a user's platform access role. Emits
 ROLE_CHANGED across the cross-plane bridge so the money plane mirrors it. Echoes
 the role now in effect.

Update the caller's own editable profile fields (full-replace of the set in
 UpdateProfileRequest). Identity/auth fields (email, status) are not editable here.

performance.title: performance
performance.description: what would crystallize at today's NAV

high_water_mark.title: high_water_mark
high_water_mark.description: the investor's own mark — why their fee differs

banking.v1.AccruedFees.title: AccruedFees
banking.v1.AccruedFees.description: What a holding owes right now. `configured` is false when the fund charges no fee.

user_id.title: user_id
user_id.description:
The target: the CONCIERGE user id (the handle the operator console carries from
 the identity plane's ListUsers) or the banking user id. Resolution is
 concierge-first via the bridge mirror (`users.concierge_user_id`), falling back
 to the banking id (existing money-plane callers stay valid); an id matching
 neither returns NOT_FOUND — never an authoritative zero.

service.title: service
service.description: the slug — the id used by every FundsService RPC

summary.title: summary
summary.description: one-line description for the catalog card

icon.title: icon
icon.description:
Catalog glyph the client maps onto one of its SVGs. Presentation only. One of:
 fund | real_estate | trading | yield | venture | treasury | commodity | credit |
 index | arbitrage. Always populated on a response — `fund` is the default.

access.title: access
access.description:
The product's default access level: hidden | view | invest. What an investor
 with no grant holds. A registration lands on `view`.

caller_access.title: caller_access
caller_access.description:
The level the CALLER effectively holds — the higher of `access` and the caller's
 own grant, if any. Populated honestly for everyone, an `AllocationManage` holder
 included: their permission lets them read and administer the product, it does not
 make them an investor in it, so a manager's `caller_access` says what they would
 get as one. A client renders the card off `access` and the subscribe control off
 this — never off `state` alone.

backing.title: backing
backing.description:
What stands behind the units: `cash` | `in_kind`. `cash` — the units were paid for
 into the fund's claim and a redemption pays out of it. `in_kind` — the units stand
 for an asset the holders own; the fund holds no cash for them, so `Redeem` is
 refused (FAILED_PRECONDITION) and holders exit through the book. Set to `in_kind`
 automatically by the first IssueUnits on the product; only SetAllocationBacking
 takes it back to `cash`. A registration lands on `cash`.

banking.v1.Allocation.title: Allocation
banking.v1.Allocation.description:
One registered investable product. Carries no money: units, NAV and positions are
 read from FundsService against the same `service` id.

granted_by.title: granted_by
granted_by.description: the AllocationManage holder who granted it

banking.v1.AllocationAccessGrant.title: AllocationAccessGrant
banking.v1.AllocationAccessGrant.description: One investor raised above an allocation's default level.

banking.v1.AllocationClaim.title: AllocationClaim
banking.v1.AllocationClaim.description:
An allocation's cash claim (`service:<id>`), split the way every reader needs it and
 read off ONE ledger balance, so the three can never disagree: `posted` is settled,
 `reserved` is spoken for by approved payments out of it that have not settled, and
 `available = posted − reserved` is what a redemption or a new payment may take.

banking_treasury.title: banking_treasury
banking_treasury.description:
Set by `GetFundRevenue` only: banking's own treasury beside the `fee` allocation, a
 separate line because it is not the allocation's (D17) — the withdrawal fees land
 there. Absent on every allocation line of `GetTreasury`, which carries it once.

banking.v1.AllocationTreasury.title: AllocationTreasury
banking.v1.AllocationTreasury.description:
One allocation as the treasury shows it (#245): the registry's name for it, its cash,
 its supply, its price and who holds it — the same shape for a product and for the
 reserved `fee` / `fund` allocations, whose `access` is `hidden`. `nav` is a product's
 posted mark, or the computed value of a reserved allocation (its cash plus every fee
 class it holds at that product's NAV) over its supply; `nav_posted_at_unix` is 0
 while nothing under it has been marked (seed-priced). `holders` are largest first —
 people, or the `fee` allocation holding a product's fee class.

decision.title: decision
decision.description: APPROVE or REJECT. PENDING is rejected as an invalid argument.

client_ip.title: client_ip
client_ip.description: Audit only — the edge supplies these; they are never trusted for authorization.

client_ip.title: client_ip
client_ip.description: browser address as seen by the trusted proxy hop

user_agent.title: user_agent
user_agent.description: clamped to 256 bytes by the hub

intent_id.title: intent_id
intent_id.description: the wallet intent this act executes (empty before intents exist)

banking.v1.AuditContext.title: AuditContext
banking.v1.AuditContext.description:
Who asked, and from where, for an act that moves or authorises money. Filled by the BFF
 (never by a browser): recorded beside the act for the audit trail and, for `origin`, the
 input to the limit profile (a first-party origin or a scope host). `client_ip` is the
 address the trusted proxy hop saw, not a caller-supplied header. Every field may be empty
 (a caller that predates the message): the act is audited blank and, for a withdrawal, judged
 on the tighter host profile — a missing origin fails closed.

invested.title: invested
invested.description: held in fund units at NAV, the units escrowed by resting sell orders included

in_orders.title: in_orders
in_orders.description: cash escrowed by the caller's resting buy orders on the book (still theirs)

in_compartments.title: in_compartments
in_compartments.description: the caller's money in scope compartments (CompartmentService), still theirs

banking.v1.Balance.title: Balance
banking.v1.Balance.description:
The user's single, network-agnostic balance, segmented by lifecycle. Every figure is
 a TigerBeetle-authoritative decimal USDT string; total = available + in_orders +
 invested + pending_withdrawal + in_compartments.

trades.title: trades
trades.description: the latest public trades, newest first

banking.v1.BookEvent.title: BookEvent
banking.v1.BookEvent.description:
One frame of WatchBook. `orders_revision` is the book revision at which the caller's
 own orders on this allocation last changed (0 = never) — compare it with the previous
 frame's to know whether to refetch ListOpenOrders.

size.title: size
size.description: decimal units resting at this price

orders.title: orders
orders.description: how many orders make it up

banking.v1.BookLevel.title: BookLevel
banking.v1.BookLevel.description: One aggregated price level of one side.

updated_at.title: updated_at
updated_at.description: unix seconds; 0 when the product has no policy row (the defaults)

allow_unbacked_trading.title: allow_unbacked_trading
allow_unbacked_trading.description:
See SetBookPolicyRequest.allow_unbacked_trading. When true the terminal tells buyers the
 units are not backed by fund cash and cannot be redeemed — the book is their only exit.

last_side.title: last_side
last_side.description: buy | sell — the taker's side of the last trade

as_of.title: as_of
as_of.description: unix seconds the snapshot was taken

banking.v1.BookSnapshot.title: BookSnapshot
banking.v1.BookSnapshot.description:
The book as of `revision`. `bids` are best (highest) first, `asks` best (lowest)
 first. `last_price` / `last_side` describe the latest trade (empty before the first);
 `mid` and `spread` are empty unless both sides have a level. `volume_24h` is the units
 traded in the trailing day and `change_24h` the signed percent move of the last price
 against the last trade at or before 24h ago (empty when there is none). `nav` is the
 fund's current mark, carried so a ticker can show the two prices side by side.

banking.v1.Candle.title: Candle
banking.v1.Candle.description: One OHLCV bucket. `time` is the bucket's start, unix seconds.

display_name.title: display_name
display_name.description: the scope's human name, as concierge announced it

available.title: available
available.description: free to spend in the scope or move back to main

held.title: held
held.description: held by the scope's services (resting orders, pending subscriptions)

banking.v1.Compartment.title: Compartment
banking.v1.Compartment.description: One compartment of the caller. Decimal USDT strings; total = available + held.

failure_reason.title: failure_reason
failure_reason.description: set only when `failed`: `insufficient_funds`, or `parked:<kind>` when the hub could not post it

payload_hash.title: payload_hash
payload_hash.description:
Hex SHA-256 over the canonical terms. Shown (short prefix) in the mail so an owner
 can tell that what they approved is what will execute.

owner_count.title: owner_count
owner_count.description: N — owners at open. The threshold is frozen from this, never recomputed later.

approvals.title: approvals
approvals.description: Votes that are still valid: an approver who has since lost ownership does not count.

executed_withdrawal_id.title: executed_withdrawal_id
executed_withdrawal_id.description:
Set exactly once, on EXECUTED — and exactly ONE of the effect ids is
 (`executed_withdrawal_id`, `executed_payment_id`, `executed_valuation_id`,
 `executed_fee_policy_change_id`, `executed_issuance_id`, `executed_subscription_id`),
 because a consilium has one effect. `consilium_execution_is_recorded` states that to
 the database as `num_nonnulls(...) = 1`.

version.title: version
version.description:
Monotonic per consilium. The live page watches this and refetches when it moves —
 the socket carries a version, never a tally.

executed_payment_id.title: executed_payment_id
executed_payment_id.description: The payment order an executed PAYMENT consilium carried.

valuation_override.title: valuation_override
valuation_override.description: A terms sibling — see the "exactly one" note above.

executed_valuation_id.title: executed_valuation_id
executed_valuation_id.description: The `fund_valuations` row an executed VALUATION-OVERRIDE consilium recorded.

fee_policy.title: fee_policy
fee_policy.description: The fourth terms sibling — set exactly for a FEE_POLICY consilium.

executed_fee_policy_change_id.title: executed_fee_policy_change_id
executed_fee_policy_change_id.description: The fee-policy change an executed FEE_POLICY consilium scheduled.

holder_grant.title: holder_grant
holder_grant.description: The fifth terms sibling — set exactly for a HOLDER_GRANT consilium.

seed_capital.title: seed_capital
seed_capital.description: The sixth — set exactly for a SEED_CAPITAL consilium.

executed_issuance_id.title: executed_issuance_id
executed_issuance_id.description:
The in-kind issuance an executed HOLDER_GRANT consilium minted
 (`AllocationsService.UnitIssuance`).

executed_subscription_id.title: executed_subscription_id
executed_subscription_id.description:
The `fund` subscription an executed SEED_CAPITAL consilium booked
 (`FundsService.Subscription`).

change_id.title: change_id
change_id.description:
The change this quorum authorizes. Inside the hashed subject, so an approval of one
 change is never a valid signature over another naming the same numbers.

allocation_name.title: allocation_name
allocation_name.description: The product's display name, read live from the registry.

from_configured.title: from_configured
from_configured.description:
The terms in force when the change was proposed. `from_configured` is false when the
 fund charged nothing — a different fact from a policy whose rates are zero — and the
 `from_*` fields are then zero / default.

effective_from.title: effective_from
effective_from.description:
Unix seconds the requester asked the change to bind from; 0 = as soon as the notice
 allows. The moment actually fixed is never earlier than 24h after the carrying vote
 while anyone holds units.

holder_count.title: holder_count
holder_count.description: How many investors hold units right now — who the change binds.

reason.title: reason
reason.description: Why, in the requester's words. Required for this kind, shown verbatim.

banking.v1.ConsiliumFeePolicyTerms.title: ConsiliumFeePolicyTerms
banking.v1.ConsiliumFeePolicyTerms.description:
The immutable subject of a FEE-POLICY consilium — a change of a product's fee terms
 that tightens them beyond the house envelope (docs/FEES.md § "Changing the terms").
 Not a money move: carrying it schedules the change, and the fee sweeper promotes it once
 the holders' notice period has run.

voter_email.title: voter_email
voter_email.description:
The recipient's own masked address, so they can confirm the mail reached the right
 seat before typing the code.

decision.title: decision
decision.description: This seat's own answer, so a reopened link shows what was already said.

attempts_remaining.title: attempts_remaining
attempts_remaining.description: Code attempts left before the token burns.

banking.v1.ConsiliumInvitation.title: ConsiliumInvitation
banking.v1.ConsiliumInvitation.description:
What the emailed owner is shown BEFORE they vote. Deliberately narrower than
 `Consilium`: no other owner's identity, no vote-by-vote breakdown.

payment_id.title: payment_id
payment_id.description:
The order this quorum authorizes. Inside the hashed subject too, so an approval of one
 payment is never a valid signature over another with identical terms.

tier.title: tier
tier.description: internal | service | external — DERIVED from the destination, never supplied.

destination.title: destination
destination.description:
Where it lands. An external destination is rendered in FULL, address and rail: a
 truncated address in an approval flow is an invitation to approve the wrong one.

amount.title: amount
amount.description: Decimal USDT string, as everywhere else on this wire.

reason.title: reason
reason.description: Why, in the initiator's words. Required, shown verbatim, never interpreted.

banking.v1.ConsiliumPaymentTerms.title: ConsiliumPaymentTerms
banking.v1.ConsiliumPaymentTerms.description:
The immutable subject of a PAYMENT consilium — the §3 rule that money pooled in an
 allocation (`service:<id>`, the reserved `fee` and `fund` included) moves only on the
 owners' quorum, at every tier.

 A PROJECTION OF THE ORDER, not the order. `banking.v1.Payment` (payments.proto) is what
 the payments screen reads; this is what an owner needs in order to judge one request:
 where the money leaves from, where it lands, how much, and why. The two ends are rendered
 as LABELS rather than as `(kind, id)` pairs because the question an owner is answering is
 "should this money move", and an account id is not an answer to it.

banking.v1.ConsiliumState.title: ConsiliumState
banking.v1.ConsiliumState.description: Where a consilium stands. Terminal everywhere except OPEN.

email.title: email
email.description: Masked (`a***@example.com`) on every surface a non-owner can reach.

notified.title: notified
notified.description: True once the mail has actually been handed to the delivery queue.

banking.v1.ConsiliumVoter.title: ConsiliumVoter
banking.v1.ConsiliumVoter.description: One owner's seat in a consilium.

created_at.title: created_at
created_at.description: unix seconds the hub recorded the credit

banking.v1.Deposit.title: Deposit
banking.v1.Deposit.description: A confirmed on-chain deposit credited to the caller's unified balance.

min_confirmations.title: min_confirmations
min_confirmations.description: confirmations before a deposit is credited

is_testnet.title: is_testnet
is_testnet.description:
Whether this rail is on testnet — the client uses it to render the correct address
 form (e.g. TON's testnet-tagged user-friendly address). Only meaningful per rail; false
 for a mainnet rail.

banking.v1.DepositScanCursor.title: DepositScanCursor
banking.v1.DepositScanCursor.description:
Seconds since a rail's deposit watcher last advanced/touched its per-network scan
 cursor (refreshed only by a completed scan cycle, so age ≈ time since the last
 healthy cycle; thresholds are the consumer's concern).

network.title: network
network.description: Rail the payment ships on (BEP20 / POLYGON / TRC20 / TON).

address.title: address
address.description: Destination address, rendered in FULL wherever a human approves it.

reason.title: reason
reason.description: operator note (audit only)

nav.title: nav
nav.description: the price the charge was measured and taken at

debt_opening.title: debt_opening
debt_opening.description: uncollected fee carried INTO this charge

debt_carried.title: debt_carried
debt_carried.description: what deferred to the next charge

high_water_mark.title: high_water_mark
high_water_mark.description: the investor's mark AFTER this charge

banking.v1.FeeAssessment.title: FeeAssessment
banking.v1.FeeAssessment.description:
One charge against one holding. `due` and `charged_cash` differ exactly when the
 holding could not cover the charge and the rest deferred into `debt_carried`.

performance_bps.title: performance_bps
performance_bps.description: 2000 = 20% of the gain above the mark

hurdle_bps.title: hurdle_bps
hurdle_bps.description: 0 = no hurdle; else the p.a. rate the gain must clear first

basis.title: basis
basis.description:
invested_capital | market_value — what the management fee is charged on.
 `invested_capital` (the default) is the cash the investor actually put in: it does
 not swell with a mark the operator posted, which keeps the fee the operator earns
 independent of the input the operator supplies.

crystallization.title: crystallization
crystallization.description:
monthly | quarterly | semi_annual | annual — how often the performance fee
 crystallizes and the mark ratchets. This is a price, not a detail: crystallizing
 more often measurably raises what an investor pays over a fund's life, because
 each reset locks in gains a later loss can no longer claw back.

version.title: version
version.description: Which version of the fund's history these terms are; 0 when unconfigured.

effective_from.title: effective_from
effective_from.description: Unix seconds since which these terms bind; 0 when unconfigured.

pending.title: pending
pending.description:
The change on its way, if any — awaiting the owners or scheduled. Shown to holders
 and non-holders alike: the terms coming are part of deciding whether to stay in.

banking.v1.FeePolicy.title: FeePolicy
banking.v1.FeePolicy.description:
One fund's fee terms. `configured` is false when the product has no policy at all,
 which is different from a policy whose rates happen to be zero.

effective_from.title: effective_from
effective_from.description:
Unix seconds the terms bind from. Provisional while awaiting the owners; fixed when
 the change is scheduled.

consilium_id.title: consilium_id
consilium_id.description: The consilium this change waits on (or waited on); empty for an administrator's change.

scheduled_at.title: scheduled_at
scheduled_at.description: Unix seconds the notice clock started; 0 while awaiting the owners.

applied_at.title: applied_at
applied_at.description: Unix seconds the terms took effect; 0 until they did.

reason.title: reason
reason.description: Why, in the requester's words; empty when none was given.

notices_waived_by.title: notices_waived_by
notices_waived_by.description:
The operator's acknowledgement of holders who could not be told (see
 AcknowledgeUndeliveredNotices): who took responsibility — the latest to, when the
 record was extended — governance detail, shown to operators and blank for everyone
 else.

notices_waived_at.title: notices_waived_at
notices_waived_at.description:
Unix seconds the (latest) acknowledgement was given; 0 when the notices were never
 waived. Public like every other moment on the change.

notices_waived_users.title: notices_waived_users
notices_waived_users.description:
The ids of the holders whose notice the mailer had given up on by that moment — the
 holders the change binds over untold. Operators only; empty for everyone else.

undelivered_notices.title: undelivered_notices
undelivered_notices.description:
Notices of this change not yet delivered to a CURRENT holder, how many of those the
 mailer has given up on — the figures a tightening waits on — and how many of the
 given-up ones the acknowledgement does not cover (all of them while there is none):
 the holders a (further) AcknowledgeUndeliveredNotices would name, so it is worth
 offering exactly while this is non-zero. Counted only while `scheduled` (0 in every
 other state), and shown to operators only.

banking.v1.FeePolicyChange.title: FeePolicyChange
banking.v1.FeePolicyChange.description:
One row of a fund's fee-policy history. `state` is one of awaiting_consilium |
 scheduled | active | superseded | rejected | cancelled; `requirement` is admin |
 owner_consilium. See docs/FEES.md § "Changing the terms".

banking.v1.FeeShares.title: FeeShares
banking.v1.FeeShares.description: The `fee` allocation's uncollected fee units in one fund — the product's fee class.

aum.title: aum
aum.description: last posted AUM (decimal USDT; empty if seed)

units_outstanding.title: units_outstanding
units_outstanding.description: decimal units in circulation (the NAV denominator)

posted_at.title: posted_at
posted_at.description: unix seconds of the mark (0 = seed)

unit_cap.title: unit_cap
unit_cap.description:
The allocation's authorised unit supply and what is left of it. `remaining_capacity`
 counts in-flight mints as issued, so a client that offers it can never offer more
 than Subscribe will accept. decimal units

remaining_capacity.title: remaining_capacity
remaining_capacity.description: decimal units still issuable (0 once at the cap)

banking.v1.FundNav.title: FundNav
banking.v1.FundNav.description:
The current price of a fund's share, derived (AUM / units_outstanding) and frozen
 between operator marks. `posted_at` is 0 when the fund has never been marked (seed
 NAV 1.0); `stale` is true when the latest mark is older than the dealing window.

banking.v1.FundNavHistory.title: FundNavHistory
banking.v1.FundNavHistory.description:
A fund's valuation log over the requested window (oldest first), and the caller's
 participation through it. `participation` steps at every mark and every change to the
 caller's units (subscribe, redeem, fee charge, in-kind issuance, book fill) and always
 ends at the window's end — "now" unless `to` was given — priced off the live holding,
 so the last point equals the position card. Empty `marks` means the fund is still on
 the seed NAV (or no mark fell in the window); it is not an error. `truncated` is true
 when more marks fell in the window than the cap allows and the OLDEST were dropped.

depth.title: depth
depth.description: price levels a side; 0 = the server default (20); capped at 50

token.title: token
token.description: The opaque single-use token from the mail. Never the code.

token.title: token
token.description: The opaque single-use token from the mail. Never the code.

operation_id.title: operation_id
operation_id.description: The operation id: a lowercase UUID, the tail of the approval's `pending_operation:<id>`.

level.title: level
level.description: view | invest (never hidden — a grant only ever adds)

request_id.title: request_id
request_id.description: a lowercase uuid, from the service's grant link

idempotency_key.title: idempotency_key
idempotency_key.description: 1..128 chars; a repeat returns the original mandate

banking.v1.GrantMandateRequest.title: GrantMandateRequest
banking.v1.GrantMandateRequest.description:
The caps are decimal USDT. What counts against them is the client's draws on the caller's
 compartment in the scope — under this mandate and any it replaced, so granting again
 never resets a cap: a hold counts at its full amount from when it is placed, until it is
 voided or expires, when only what was captured of it still counts; a capture of a hold
 placed more than 24 h ago counts from when it is made.

allocation.title: allocation
allocation.description: fee | fund — a reserved allocation only

user_id.title: user_id
user_id.description:
On the request: a banking (or concierge) user id, resolved the way every admin RPC
 resolves a target. On a response: the money-plane id the terms stored.

banking.v1.HolderGrantTerms.title: HolderGrantTerms
banking.v1.HolderGrantTerms.description:
The immutable subject of a HOLDER-GRANT consilium (#245): `units` of the reserved
 `allocation` minted to `user_id`, with no cash leg. The units are frozen, not a cash
 figure — what they are worth is the allocation's NAV at execution. Executing it records
 a `UnitIssuance` (`source = "mint"`, holder `user`) that `executed_issuance_id` names.

user_id.title: user_id
user_id.description:
Who receives the units: a banking (or concierge) user id, resolved the way every
 admin RPC resolves a target. Required — a mint to nobody is a malformed request.
 Only a person: the company is not a holder (#245), and a reserved allocation is
 seated by the owners' consilium (`ConsiliumService.OpenHolderGrant`) or by the fee
 accrual, never by an operator's mint — so there is deliberately no arm for either.

cost_basis.title: cost_basis
cost_basis.description:
Decimal USDT the holder is deemed to have paid. Empty means `units × NAV` at the
 dealing mark — what a subscription for these units would have cost right now. An
 explicit value may be anything, zero included: a stake in an asset the holder
 already owned cost them no cash. This is what lands in their position's cost basis,
 and so what their P&L and management fee are measured from.

concierge_user_id.title: concierge_user_id
concierge_user_id.description:
The concierge canonical user id (a UUID) of the already-authenticated user. Banking
 maps it to its local mirror row (provisioned by the cross-plane bridge) and mints the
 money-plane pair for that user. Banking never sees Google's `sub` — the bridge carries
 it; the BFF carries this concierge id, which it has from the concierge sign-in.

user_agent.title: user_agent
user_agent.description:
Device metadata captured by the BFF at sign-in, stored on the refresh-token family
 for the "sessions & devices" surface. Best-effort, free-form.

banking.v1.Jwk.title: Jwk
banking.v1.Jwk.description:
One JSON Web Key. Ed25519 keys are OKP: kty="OKP", crv="Ed25519", x=base64url
 public key, alg="EdDSA". `kid` is a stable thumbprint of the public key.

include_unlisted.title: include_unlisted
include_unlisted.description:
Include `draft`, `closed` and `hidden` allocations. Requires AllocationManage; a
 caller without it is refused rather than silently downgraded to the visible list.

banking.v1.ListFundNavHistoryRequest.title: ListFundNavHistoryRequest
banking.v1.ListFundNavHistoryRequest.description:
Keyed by the ALLOCATION (the product's registry key — today equal to the service id)
 rather than the service, so a hidden allocation such as the fee fund can serve its
 holders' history later without a second route. `from`/`to` are unix seconds,
 inclusive; 0 means "from the first mark" / "up to now".

limit.title: limit
limit.description: Rows to return. 0 means the server default (100); the server caps it at 200.

party.title: party
party.description: Either end. Unset means every party.

fund_owned_only.title: fund_owned_only
fund_owned_only.description:
Only orders whose source is an allocation's claim (`service:<id>`) or banking's
 treasury — the ones the owners' consilium gates, i.e. the governance surface.

offset.title: offset
offset.description: Lines to skip, in the order they are paid. Past the end is an empty page.

limit.title: limit
limit.description: Lines to return. 0 means the server default (50); the server caps it at 200.

refresh_token.title: refresh_token
refresh_token.description: The caller's current refresh token: proves identity and flags the current session.

revoke_all.title: revoke_all
revoke_all.description:
When true, bump the user's token_version (coarse "revoke all"), not just this
 refresh family.

used_24h.title: used_24h
used_24h.description: drawn in the rolling 24 h, decimal USDT

outstanding.title: outstanding
outstanding.description: held by the client's active holds now

book_filled_24h.title: book_filled_24h
book_filled_24h.description: sent to other users in the rolling 24 h

replaced_at.title: replaced_at
replaced_at.description: 0 unless a later grant replaced it; then `outstanding` is its own holds'

banking.v1.MandateOperation.title: MandateOperation
banking.v1.MandateOperation.description: What a mandate lets the service do with the caller's compartment.

expires_at.title: expires_at
expires_at.description: unix seconds: until when this request can be granted

banking.v1.MandateRequest.title: MandateRequest
banking.v1.MandateRequest.description: What a service asks the caller to grant, as banking stored it. Amounts are decimal USDT.

old_address.title: old_address
old_address.description: the retired address — kept so the operator can watch it

new_address.title: new_address
new_address.description: the NEW fundable, custody-held deposit address

to_scope.title: to_scope
to_scope.description: the other side; one of the two must be `main`

idempotency_key.title: idempotency_key
idempotency_key.description: client-minted (a UUID per click); a repeat returns the original move

banking.v1.NavMark.title: NavMark
banking.v1.NavMark.description:
One operator valuation mark, as posted. Same figures as FundNav, without the live
 supply/capacity fields that only make sense for the current mark.

withdrawable.title: withdrawable
withdrawable.description: max requestable on this rail (= available)

withdrawal_fee.title: withdrawal_fee
withdrawal_fee.description: flat network fee retained on a withdrawal

banking.v1.NetworkWithdrawable.title: NetworkWithdrawable
banking.v1.NetworkWithdrawable.description:
Per-rail withdrawal options (the accept-and-queue UX). `withdrawable` is the whole
 available balance (a request beyond `instant` is accepted and queued); `instant` is
 the portion that ships without queueing = min(available, rail liquidity).

reason.title: reason
reason.description:
Required. Bounded at 500 bytes, no control characters; it is INSIDE the hashed
 payload the approver signs.

id.title: id
id.description:
Unique within the feed: the aggregate UUID for a withdrawal / subscription /
 redemption, the on-chain `tx_ref` for a deposit (which has no surrogate id).

state.title: state
state.description:
Lifecycle, per kind. deposit: always `credited` (the row exists only once the
 watcher has confirmed it). subscription: always `completed` (an immutable mint).
 withdrawal: queued | processing | completed | failed | cancelled.
 redemption: queued | completed | failed | cancelled.
 fee: `charged` when the whole charge was collected, `partly_deferred` when the
 holding could not cover it and the rest was carried as debt to the next charge.

created_at.title: created_at
created_at.description: unix seconds the hub recorded the operation

amount.title: amount
amount.description:
Cash moved, as a magnitude — the sign is implied by `kind`, never encoded here.
 Empty for a redemption that has not settled yet (settle-time pricing).

net_amount.title: net_amount
net_amount.description: withdrawal only — amount − fee, what ships on-chain

units.title: units
units.description: fund kinds — units minted (subscription) or burned (redemption)

nav.title: nav
nav.description: fund kinds — price dealt at (empty until a redemption settles)

network.title: network
network.description: rail kinds — bep20 | polygon | trc20 | ton

tx_ref.title: tx_ref
tx_ref.description: rail kinds — the on-chain reference (empty until settled)

management.title: management
management.description:
fee only — the two legs of the charge, so the row can say WHY it was taken rather
 than only how much. `management` is rent on parked capital and is charged whether
 the fund gained or not; `performance` is the share of the gain above this
 investor's own high-water mark, and is zero except at a crystallization.

scope.title: scope
scope.description:
The wallet compartment the row belongs to: `main` for every kind this feed carries
 today (deposits and withdrawals are main's; fund subscriptions, redemptions and fees
 settle against main's balance). A client in scope mode keeps only the rows whose
 `scope` is its own; compartment moves and scope payouts are not in this feed yet.

banking.v1.Operation.title: Operation
banking.v1.Operation.description:
One row of the timeline. `kind` is the discriminator — it decides which of the
 remaining fields carry a value; the rest are empty. Deliberately flat rather than a
 oneof: the whole surface is projected to TypeScript through OpenAPI, where a flat
 message with a documented discriminator survives the pipeline unambiguously.

 | field        | deposit | withdrawal | subscription | redemption | fee        |
 | ------------ | ------- | ---------- | ------------ | ---------- | ---------- |
 | amount       | ✓       | ✓ (gross)  | ✓ (cash in)  | ✓ at settle| ✓ (taken)  |
 | fee          |         | ✓          |              |            |            |
 | net_amount   |         | ✓          |              |            |            |
 | units / nav  |         |            | ✓            | ✓ at settle| ✓          |
 | service      |         |            | ✓            | ✓          | ✓          |
 | network      | ✓       | ✓          |              |            |            |
 | address      |         | ✓          |              |            |            |
 | tx_ref       | ✓       | ✓ at settle|              |            |            |
 | management   |         |            |              |            | ✓          |
 | performance  |         |            |              |            | ✓          |

 The `fee` row is the one the investor did not initiate: the fund charging its own
 management and performance fee against the holding. It moves no cash and touches no
 chain — units are clawed back to the manager on the share ledger — so `amount` is what
 those units were WORTH at `nav`, not a transfer. Without this row an investor's units
 would simply shrink with nothing on the timeline to explain it.

truncated.title: truncated
truncated.description:
True when the caller's history is longer than `limit` — the client is looking at
 the newest page, not the whole record.

avg_fill_price.title: avg_fill_price
avg_fill_price.description: decimal USDT per unit; empty until the first fill

fee_paid.title: fee_paid
fee_paid.description: decimal USDT the caller paid as taker on this order

reject_reason.title: reject_reason
reject_reason.description: free text; set exactly when state = rejected

cancel_reason.title: cancel_reason
cancel_reason.description:
Set exactly when state = cancelled: "" | user | ioc_remainder | market_remainder.
 `user` is the owner's own cancel; the other two are the hub cancelling what an IOC
 limit / a market order could not fill at once — such an order may still show
 `filled > 0`, which is what makes the reason worth carrying.

banking.v1.Order.title: Order
banking.v1.Order.description:
One order. `price` is the limit — for a market order, the limit the hub derived from
 the quote at placement. `filled`, `remaining`, `avg_fill_price` and `fee_paid` grow as
 fills land; `state` ends in `filled`, `cancelled` or `rejected` (`reject_reason` set —
 the ledger refused the escrow after the order was recorded, a raced over-spend the
 optimistic balance check could not see). `user_id` is populated only on the caller's
 own orders.

banking.v1.ParkedEvent.title: ParkedEvent
banking.v1.ParkedEvent.description:
One parked outbox row. `reason` is the relay's last error; `parked_at` is unix
 seconds; `compensated` marks a half-applied event that is owed compensation
 (never unparkable).

banking.v1.ParticipationPoint.title: ParticipationPoint
banking.v1.ParticipationPoint.description:
The value of the caller's holding at one instant: the units they held then × the
 NAV in force then (the seed NAV 1.0 before the first mark).

kind.title: kind
kind.description:
user | service | treasury. (`piggybank` and `revenue` are retired, #245 — the platform's
 money is the `fee` and `fund` allocations: `{kind: "service", id: "fee" | "fund"}`.)
 `treasury` is banking's own (D17), never a destination, and closed as a source until
 concierge's scope approvals decide its spending (D24); its id is empty or
 `main:treasury`.

id.title: id
id.description:
A service slug for `service` (`fee` and `fund` included). For `user`, the CONCIERGE
 user id the console carries (resolved to the money-plane id here; a banking id is
 accepted as a fallback, the way UsersService.GetUserBalance resolves one).

banking.v1.Party.title: Party
banking.v1.Party.description: One end of a payment, as a REQUEST names it.

pay_from.title: pay_from
pay_from.description: `main`, or the invoice's scope (the caller's compartment there)

state.title: state
state.description:
open | processing | paid | cancelled | expired. `paid` only once the ledger has posted
 the payment; `processing` until then (it ends as `paid`, or back at `open` if refused).

paid_at.title: paid_at
paid_at.description: unix seconds, once paid (posted), to the payer only

available_main.title: available_main
available_main.description:
What the caller could pay from right now, decimal USDT: their `main` available
 balance and their available balance in this scope's compartment.

tier.title: tier
tier.description: internal | service | external — DERIVED from the destination, never supplied.

amount.title: amount
amount.description: Decimal USDT string, as everywhere else on this wire.

reason.title: reason
reason.description: Why, in the initiator's words. Required, shown verbatim, never interpreted.

requirement.title: requirement
requirement.description: owner_consilium | subject_consent — the one requirement, read off the source.

payload_hash.title: payload_hash
payload_hash.description: Hex SHA-256 over the canonical terms, re-verified at execution.

consilium_id.title: consilium_id
consilium_id.description: Set exactly when the requirement is the owner consilium.

consent.title: consent
consent.description: Set exactly when the requirement is the subject's consent.

executed_withdrawal_id.title: executed_withdrawal_id
executed_withdrawal_id.description:
Set on EXECUTED for an external order only: an internal one settled as a ledger
 transfer and records no id of its own.

seat.title: seat
seat.description:
The seat that decides the order: `consilium`, `consent` (the emailed token),
 `concierge_approval` (a `bank:payment` approval) or `session` (the investor's answer in
 the cabinet). Empty only for a row written before seats were recorded.

approval_id.title: approval_id
approval_id.description: Concierge's id of the approval, once banking has opened it; set for `concierge_approval`.

session_decision.title: session_decision
session_decision.description: The investor's own answer, set for `session`.

payload_hash.title: payload_hash
payload_hash.description: Hex SHA-256 over the canonical terms the answer binds to.

decision.title: decision
decision.description: This seat's own answer; PENDING until they give one.

invalidated.title: invalidated
invalidated.description:
True when one of the pins recorded at open has moved: the order can no longer be
 answered or executed.

banking.v1.PaymentConfirmation.title: PaymentConfirmation
banking.v1.PaymentConfirmation.description:
One order as the investor it spends is shown it: the terms they answer and nothing about
 the operator beyond a masked address.

notified.title: notified
notified.description: True once the consent mail has actually been handed to concierge.

attempts_remaining.title: attempts_remaining
attempts_remaining.description: Code attempts left before the token burns.

invalidated.title: invalidated
invalidated.description:
True when one of the pins recorded at open (the subject's token version, their
 mailbox) has moved: the seat can no longer be answered or executed.

banking.v1.PaymentConsent.title: PaymentConsent
banking.v1.PaymentConsent.description: The consent seat of an investor-sourced order, as the owner surface sees it.

subject_email.title: subject_email
subject_email.description:
The recipient's own masked address, so they can confirm the mail reached the right
 mailbox before typing the code.

decision.title: decision
decision.description: This seat's own answer, so a reopened link shows what was already said.

attempts_remaining.title: attempts_remaining
attempts_remaining.description: Code attempts left before the token burns.

banking.v1.PaymentConsentInvitation.title: PaymentConsentInvitation
banking.v1.PaymentConsentInvitation.description:
What the emailed investor is shown BEFORE they answer. Deliberately narrower than
 `Payment`: the terms they are consenting to, and nothing about the operator beyond a
 masked address.

banking.v1.PaymentDestination.title: PaymentDestination
banking.v1.PaymentDestination.description:
Where a payment lands. An external SOURCE is unrepresentable on purpose: money cannot
 arrive from an address by anyone's say-so — that is a deposit, which a chain watcher
 attests.

kind.title: kind
kind.description: service | user | treasury, or `external` for an address.

id.title: id
id.description:
The service slug, or the MONEY-PLANE user id (the request accepts a concierge id; the
 response carries what the order stored). Empty for addresses.

detail.title: detail
detail.description:
What a person recognises this end BY, beside the label: the receiving investor's
