 MASKED mailbox for `user`, the product's title for `service`. Empty otherwise. Never
 part of the digest — the label is what an approval binds.

banking.v1.PaymentEnd.title: PaymentEnd
banking.v1.PaymentEnd.description:
One end of a payment, as a RESPONSE describes it. `label` is the wording every approval
 surface (the owners' mail, the subject's mail, this screen) shares; the structured
 fields let a screen link to the account.

banking.v1.PaymentState.title: PaymentState
banking.v1.PaymentState.description: Where an order stands. Terminal everywhere except PENDING and APPROVED.

total.title: total
total.description: Canonical decimal USDT; the sum of ALL lines, not of this page.

max_line.title: max_line
max_line.description: The largest single line, as the approval shows it.

recipients.title: recipients
recipients.description: How many lines the payout has in all.

recipients_without_history.title: recipients_without_history
recipients_without_history.description: How many of them are recipients without history in the scope.

lines_digest.title: lines_digest
lines_digest.description:
SHA-256 over the lines, as stored with the operation. The hub recomputes it from the
 lines it reads and refuses the page when they differ.

offset.title: offset
offset.description: The page asked for, echoed so a client can tell which one it holds.

line_no.title: line_no
line_no.description: The place in the payout, from 0.

recipient.title: recipient
recipient.description: The recipient as the requesting service named them — the string `lines_digest` covers.

no_history.title: no_history
no_history.description:
The recipient has no earlier POSTED approved payout in this scope: banking has never
 paid them through an approval here, so an approver has nothing to compare the line with.
 Pending payouts do not count (they may still fail), nor do the service's automatic
 payouts (redemption, book, fee rebate) or this operation's own.

banking.v1.PayoutReviewLine.title: PayoutReviewLine
banking.v1.PayoutReviewLine.description: One recipient and what they are paid.

tif.title: tif
tif.description: gtc | ioc | alo (post-only); market orders are always ioc

price.title: price
price.description: decimal USDT per unit, on the tick; EMPTY for market

client_order_id.title: client_order_id
client_order_id.description: required, 1..64 chars, unique per caller (the retry key)

units.title: units
units.description: units held free in the holding (decimal)

cost_basis.title: cost_basis
cost_basis.description: net cash invested, average cost (decimal USDT)

nav_as_of.title: nav_as_of
nav_as_of.description: unix seconds of the NAV mark (0 = seed NAV)

units_in_orders.title: units_in_orders
units_in_orders.description:
Units committed to the holder's resting sell orders on the book (BookService).
 Still theirs — `value` and `pnl` price `units + units_in_orders` — but not free to
 redeem or sell again until the order fills or is cancelled.

banking.v1.Position.title: Position
banking.v1.Position.description:
A user's holding in one fund. `value = (units + units_in_orders) × nav`; `pnl = value − cost_basis`
 (a signed decimal — losses are negative). `nav_as_of` is the unix-seconds timestamp
 of the NAV mark used (0 when the fund is on the bootstrap seed NAV).

aum.title: aum
aum.description: decimal USDT — the fund's total assets under management

custody.title: custody
custody.description: liquid on-chain USDT held in this rail's custody wallet

treasury_address.title: treasury_address
treasury_address.description: the rail's hot wallet — fund USDT (liquidity) + gas here

onchain_usdt.title: onchain_usdt
onchain_usdt.description: decimal USDT actually on-chain in the treasury wallet

onchain_gas.title: onchain_gas
onchain_gas.description: decimal native units (BNB | TRX | TON) for gas

gas_station_address.title: gas_station_address
gas_station_address.description:
The rail's sweep GAS-STATION wallet — a separate account paying the gas drops
 that consolidate user deposits into the treasury. Fund the native coin here,
 never USDT. Empty when the rail has no gas-station view.

is_testnet.title: is_testnet
is_testnet.description:
Whether the addresses above are testnet-tagged, so a client can render them in the
 rail's user-facing form (e.g. TON's testnet-tagged friendly address). Only
 meaningful per rail; false where the rail's address form is network-agnostic.

banking.v1.RailLiquidity.title: RailLiquidity
banking.v1.RailLiquidity.description:
Per-rail on-chain liquidity (the treasury / Layer 2). The `treasury_*`/`onchain_*`
 fields are the operator funding view, read best-effort from the chain — empty means
 the rail is unconfigured or the read was unavailable, never an error.

scan_cursors.title: scan_cursors
scan_cursors.description:
Per-rail deposit-scan diagnostics; only configured rails appear. A large age on
 a configured rail means the deposit scan is stalled — deposits confirm on-chain
 but are not credited. Diagnostics only: it does NOT gate `ready`.

unseal_failures.title: unseal_failures
unseal_failures.description:
Signer unseal failures seen on money-moving paths (sweep / withdrawal signing)
 since this instance booted. Any non-zero value means a PROVABLY DEAD key (the
 KEK-epoch bug class) was asked to sign — funds on its address cannot move.
 Diagnostics only: it does NOT gate `ready`.

banking.v1.ReadinessResponse.title: ReadinessResponse
banking.v1.ReadinessResponse.description:
`ready` is the gate the orchestrator acts on; the rest are diagnostics so a
 not-ready response says *why* without scraping logs. `parked_rows` are outbox
 events the relay could not apply (need operator intervention); `backlog` is the
 count of undispatched rows and the age of the oldest, surfacing a wedged relay.

network.title: network
network.description: bep20 | polygon | trc20 | ton — the rail it arrived on

expected_amount.title: expected_amount
expected_amount.description:
Optional operator assertion in decimal USDT. When set it must equal what the chain
 reports or the call is refused, so a mistyped reference fails loudly instead of
 silently crediting some other transfer.

banking.v1.RecordDepositRequest.title: RecordDepositRequest
banking.v1.RecordDepositRequest.description:
Record an arrival that reached a rail out of band, PROVEN against the chain.

 The caller supplies only a pointer to a fact: the reference is read back from the chain
 and the amount and the credited party are taken from what is actually there. An operator
 therefore cannot mint a balance by typing one — the worst a wrong reference can do is
 name a transfer that does not exist, or one that did not land on an address of ours,
 and both are rejected.

recorded.title: recorded
recorded.description: false if `tx_ref` was already recorded (idempotent no-op)

amount.title: amount
amount.description: what the CHAIN reported, decimal USDT — never the caller's number

banking.v1.RecordDepositResponse.title: RecordDepositResponse
banking.v1.RecordDepositResponse.description:
The chain names the owner of the deposit address the transfer landed on, so the
 credited party is always a PERSON: `party_kind` is `user` and `party_id` their banking
 id. A transfer to the treasury address is nobody's until the owners say whose — it is
 refused here and attributed through `SeedCapital`.

banking.v1.Redemption.title: Redemption
banking.v1.Redemption.description:
A redemption in the accept-and-queue saga. `units` are fixed at request; `nav`/`cash`
 are empty until settle (settle-time pricing). State ∈ {queued, completed, failed,
 cancelled}.

banking.v1.RedemptionQueueItem.title: RedemptionQueueItem
banking.v1.RedemptionQueueItem.description:
One queued redemption for the operator queue. `email` is the mirrored identity email
 (may be empty if the bridge hasn't populated it). `created_at` is unix seconds.

icon.title: icon
icon.description:
See `Allocation.icon`. Empty means "not chosen" and lands on `fund`; a value
 outside the set is refused rather than silently defaulted. Deliberately NOT
 `optional`, unlike the update request: a registration creates the row, so there is
 no earlier pick that "unset" could destroy — absent and empty both legitimately
 mean "the operator chose nothing yet", which is what the default is for.

network.title: network
network.description: bep20 | polygon | trc20 | ton — the rail to ship on

amount.title: amount
amount.description: gross decimal USDT to debit (the fee is taken from this)

idempotency_key.title: idempotency_key
idempotency_key.description:
Client-minted, 1..128 bytes, unique per user (the withdraw page mints one per load). A
 repeat with the same network, address and amount returns the first withdrawal and opens
 no second; the same key with other terms is ALREADY_EXISTS. Empty (a client that predates
 the field) = no deduplication.

user_id.title: user_id
user_id.description:
Whose units are burnt: a banking (or concierge) user id, shaped as IssueUnits'
 holder is and for the same reason. Required — a burn of nobody's units is a
 malformed request.

units.title: units
units.description: decimal units, > 0, at most what the holder has available

cost_basis.title: cost_basis
cost_basis.description:
Decimal USDT of book value written off, recorded on the row. Empty means
 `units × NAV` at the dealing mark, like IssueUnits. No cash moves either way.

idempotency_key.title: idempotency_key
idempotency_key.description: required, 1..64 chars, unique per service (shared with IssueUnits)

force.title: force
force.description:
Retiring is allowed on a `closed` allocation only; `force = true` is the operator's
 explicit override to burn units out of a live (draft or open) product.

refresh_token.title: refresh_token
refresh_token.description: The caller's current refresh token (proves identity).

session_id.title: session_id
session_id.description: The session id to revoke (must belong to the same user).

effective_from.title: effective_from
effective_from.description:
Unix seconds the change should bind from; 0 = as soon as the notice period allows.
 An earlier request than the notice allows is lifted to the minimum, not refused.

reason.title: reason
reason.description:
Why, in the requester's words. Required and non-empty when the owners must approve
 (the approval mail is refused without one); optional otherwise. Shown verbatim.

min_kyc_level.title: min_kyc_level
min_kyc_level.description: the concierge KYC level a user needs to move money in or pay the scope's invoices

max_moved_in_24h.title: max_moved_in_24h
max_moved_in_24h.description: rolling 24 h total moved in, per user

max_balance.title: max_balance
max_balance.description:
Ceiling on the compartment's total, applied ONLY to the user's own MoveFunds in —
 payouts, captures and refunds into the compartment are never refused for it.

caller_eligible.title: caller_eligible
caller_eligible.description:
Whether the CALLER meets `min_kyc_level` right now — the UI's reason to offer the
 move or to point at verification instead.

auto_payout_per_op.title: auto_payout_per_op
auto_payout_per_op.description:
Automatic ceilings, per (service client, scope): past them a payout or transfer
 needs an approval. Defaults 1000 / 5000 / 5000.

banking.v1.ScopePolicy.title: ScopePolicy
banking.v1.ScopePolicy.description:
What it takes to move money into a scope, and how far its services may move money
 without an approval. Limits are decimal USDT strings; an empty limit means none.

network.title: network
network.description: bep20 | polygon | trc20 | ton — the rail the capital lands on

expected_amount.title: expected_amount
expected_amount.description:
REQUIRED, decimal USDT: what the chain must report for this reference. A seed is
 proposed at a figure the owners approve, not at "whatever the chain says" — a
 mistyped reference naming some other real transfer fails here, loudly.

depositor_user_id.title: depositor_user_id
depositor_user_id.description:
Whose money it is: the person booked as depositor and seated as a holder of `fund`.
 A banking (or concierge) user id, resolved the way every admin RPC resolves a
 target. Empty means the caller — an owner attributing their own transfer.

banking.v1.SeedCapitalRequest.title: SeedCapitalRequest
banking.v1.SeedCapitalRequest.description:
Propose a seed: a transfer that reached a rail's treasury, PROVEN against the chain,
 as `depositor_user_id`'s deposit and subscription into `fund`.

 Like RecordDepositRequest the caller supplies only a pointer to a fact: the transfer
 must have landed on the rail's treasury address from a sender outside every wallet we
 control. A transfer to a user's deposit address is that user's deposit, not a seed —
 refused, use RecordDeposit. The sweep consolidating a user's address into the treasury
 is money already on the ledger — refused. Unlike RecordDeposit the amount is UNDER THE
 OWNERS' SIGNATURE: `expected_amount` is required, checked against the chain now, and
 frozen into the terms the owners vote over.

recorded.title: recorded
recorded.description: always false: the booking is the consilium's execution

amount.title: amount
amount.description: what the terms carry, decimal USDT — verified against the chain

banking.v1.SeedCapitalResponse.title: SeedCapitalResponse
banking.v1.SeedCapitalResponse.description:
A seed is a consilium, not a write: `recorded` is always false here — nothing is
 booked until the owners' quorum executes it — and `consilium_id` is where the
 proposal lives (`ConsiliumService.GetConsilium`).

amount.title: amount
amount.description: decimal USDT, as the chain reports it

depositor_user_id.title: depositor_user_id
depositor_user_id.description: the money-plane id the terms stored

banking.v1.SeedCapitalTerms.title: SeedCapitalTerms
banking.v1.SeedCapitalTerms.description:
The immutable subject of a SEED-CAPITAL consilium (#245): the transfer `tx_ref` names
 on `network`, which the chain must report as exactly `amount` USDT landing on the
 treasury from outside, is `depositor_user_id`'s — booked as their deposit and
 subscribed into `fund` at its price when the quorum executes. The amount is frozen
 into the terms (the owners approve "this dollar is this person's"); the units are
 not — they are what the cash buys at execution. Executing it records the fund
 subscription `executed_subscription_id` names. Opened through
 `BalanceService.SeedCapital`, never here.

current.title: current
current.description: True for the family that owns the refresh token presented on the listing call.

banking.v1.Session.title: Session
banking.v1.Session.description: One active session = one refresh-token family. Timestamps are unix SECONDS.

state.title: state
state.description: open | closed  (draft is entered only by RegisterAllocation)

market_slippage_bps.title: market_slippage_bps
market_slippage_bps.description: 0..10000; how far past the best quote a market order may fill

allow_unbacked_trading.title: allow_unbacked_trading
allow_unbacked_trading.description:
The operator's acknowledgement that the book may trade units the fund holds no cash
 for (`Allocation.backing = in_kind`): a buyer pays cash for a claim on an asset held in
 kind and cannot redeem it. Required to open the book on an in_kind product, and
 checked again on every order — the backing can flip after the book opened (the first
 in-kind mint). Harmless on a cash product. The terminal shows buyers a notice when set.

units.title: units
units.description: decimal units; empty settles the whole accumulated balance

code.description: The secret code from the same mail. Compared in constant time, as a hash.

decision.description: APPROVE or REJECT. PENDING is rejected as an invalid argument.

invitation.description: The invitation as it stands after the vote.

decided.description: True when this vote carried the consilium to its verdict.

banking.v1.Subscription.title: Subscription
banking.v1.Subscription.description:
The receipt for one subscription (mint): `cash` of the user's balance bought `units`
 at `nav`. The position itself is read via GetPosition once the relay has applied it.

banking.v1.TokenResponse.title: TokenResponse
banking.v1.TokenResponse.description:
A first-party token pair plus a snapshot of the principal. All expiries are
 unix SECONDS (matching the JWT `exp` claim); the BFF parses them with
 proto-loader `longs: String`.

taker_side.title: taker_side
taker_side.description: buy | sell — the side that crossed the spread

user_side.title: user_side
user_side.description: the caller's side; empty on the public tape

order_id.title: order_id
order_id.description: the caller's order; empty on the public tape

fee.title: fee
fee.description: decimal USDT the caller paid; empty on the public tape

banking.v1.Trade.title: Trade
banking.v1.Trade.description:
One fill. On the public tape only `id`, `service`, `price`, `size`, `taker_side` and
 `executed_at` are populated. On the caller's own tape (ListUserTrades) `user_side` is
 the caller's side, `order_id` their order on it and `fee` what they paid (empty when
 they were the maker); the counterparty is never disclosed.

bank.title: bank
bank.description: mocked USD liquidity (separate ledger; off-ramp FX)

total_custody.title: total_custody
total_custody.description: sum of rail custody — the asset side

reserved_for_withdrawals.title: reserved_for_withdrawals
reserved_for_withdrawals.description: locked by in-flight withdrawals and approved payments

held_by_users.title: held_by_users
held_by_users.description: Σ user claims — what people hold directly

banking_treasury.title: banking_treasury
banking_treasury.description:
banking's own treasury, `scope_account:main:treasury` (D17): the withdrawal fees it
 retained, less what the owners approved paying out of it.

held_in_compartments.title: held_in_compartments
held_in_compartments.description: Σ users' scope compartments — still people's

banking.v1.Treasury.title: Treasury
banking.v1.Treasury.description:
The treasury picture: per-rail liquidity (Layer 2) and who the claims on it belong to
 (Layer 1). Under the unified-claim model the invariant is GLOBAL — `total_custody`
 (the asset side) equals the sum of all claims — and every claim is somebody's (#245):
 a person's directly (`held_by_users`, Σ `user:<id>` claims; `held_in_compartments`,
 Σ their scope compartments), an allocation's, whose units people hold (`allocations`,
 the hidden `fee` and `fund` included), or banking's own (`banking_treasury`). Nothing here
 is a remainder: each figure is read off its own accounts, and whether they add up to
 the custody is the reconciliation's finding, not this view's arithmetic.

banking.v1.UnitHolderRef.title: UnitHolderRef
banking.v1.UnitHolderRef.description:
One holder of an allocation's units, as the cap table and the treasury name them.
 `kind` is `user` (`id` is the banking user id) or `allocation` (`id` is the holding
 allocation's slug — the reserved `fee` allocation holding a product's fee class). The
 reserved allocations' own holders are always people.

queued_units.title: queued_units
queued_units.description:
Decimal units of `mint` issuances still `queued` — recorded, not yet posted by the
 relay. Once they land, `units_outstanding` grows by this much, so an operator
 pinning the cap to what is issued must wait for it to read zero: a cap pinned to
 the settled figure alone leaves the queued mint to land above it.
 TODO(#271): retire (PR #278) shrinks supply — subtract queued retires once it lands.

banking.v1.UnitHolders.title: UnitHolders
banking.v1.UnitHolders.description:
The cap table of one product: the settled supply and every holder of it, largest
 first (ties by the holder's stored identity, so the table reads the same on every
 refresh). Σ `holders[].units` = `units_outstanding` is the supply invariant the
 reconciliation checks — it is read, never derived, here. All units decimal.

banking.v1.UnitHolding.title: UnitHolding
banking.v1.UnitHolding.description:
One line of a cap table: who, and how many units (decimal). Holdings of zero are not
 listed.

holder_kind.title: holder_kind
holder_kind.description:
`user` | `allocation`. (The company stake's two historical rows never cross the
 wire: a lookup that lands on one is refused as a conflict, #245.)

holder_id.title: holder_id
holder_id.description:
The banking user id for `user`; the holding allocation's slug (`fee`) for
 `allocation`. A client must never resolve an `allocation` holder as a user.

units.title: units
units.description: decimal units minted or retired (always positive)

nav.title: nav
nav.description: decimal USDT per unit the issuance was recorded at

state.title: state
state.description:
`queued` until the relay posts the leg, then `applied`. A client that needs the
 units to be visible on the ledger polls for `applied`; a `queued` row is one the
 relay has not reached yet (or one it parked — see BalanceService.ListParkedEvents).

source.title: source
source.description:
Where the units came from — or went: `mint` (IssueUnits or an executed holder
 grant — supply grew by `units`) or `retire` (RetireUnits — burnt out of the
 holder's account, supply shrank by `units`). `units` is always the magnitude; the
 source is the direction.
 Always populated; a row that predates the field reads as `mint`.

banking.v1.UnitIssuance.title: UnitIssuance
banking.v1.UnitIssuance.description:
One in-kind issuance: a mint or a retirement (`source`).
 The holder is a flattened `UnitHolderRef`: a person, or the reserved allocation the
 fee accrual minted a product's fee class to.

icon.title: icon
icon.description:
See `Allocation.icon`. `optional` — and it is the ONLY field here that is, because
 it is the only one where "the caller did not mention it" has to be distinguishable
 from "the caller cleared it". Unset means LEAVE THE STORED ICON ALONE; empty string
 means reset to `fund`; an unknown value is refused.

 Without presence a scalar `string` cannot tell those apart, and every caller built
 before this field existed — a consumer repo on an older `contracts` pin, a browser
 tab holding a stale bundle, a pod mid-rolling-deploy — would silently wipe the
 operator's pick on the next title edit. `title` and `summary` need no such escape:
 they predate every live caller, so an omitted title is a client bug the boundary
 refuses outright rather than a field it has to guess about.

banking.v1.UpdateProfileRequest.title: UpdateProfileRequest
banking.v1.UpdateProfileRequest.description:
The caller's editable profile, full-replace. Same 10 fields as the editable part of
 UserProfile; an empty string clears the field.

in_compartments.title: in_compartments
in_compartments.description: posted across the user's scope compartments

banking.v1.UserBalanceResponse.title: UserBalanceResponse
banking.v1.UserBalanceResponse.description:
A live ledger balance for a user. `amount` and `pending` are u128 minor-unit
 decimal STRINGS (proto3 has no u128; a string is lossless and matches
 proto-loader's `longs: String`). They cover the user's whole cash — the `main` claim
 plus every scope compartment, split by `main` and `in_compartments` — and each account
 is credit-normal, so `amount` (Σ posted credits − posted debits) is non-negative by
 invariant.
 `authoritative` is true when read directly from TigerBeetle; `as_of` is unix
 seconds. The `authoritative`/`as_of` pair is the forward-compat seam for a future
 read projection — a projection may later return `authoritative=false` rows with
 no breaking proto change. (Named for the users surface; the company-money
 `BalanceService` owns its own balance messages.)

legal_name.title: legal_name
legal_name.description:
Editable profile fields (control plane; empty until the user sets them). email and
 status above stay read-only — email is the IdP's, status is admin-managed.

kyc_level.title: kyc_level
kyc_level.description:
Kept wire-identical with concierge.v1.UserProfile (the cabinet TS is aliased to the
 concierge shape). The identity plane OWNS kyc/role; the money plane mirrors them for
 gating but does not re-serve them on its self-service GetMe, so these stay default
 here — the fields exist for cross-plane wire parity.

 The tier ladder, written down here because the money plane is what ENFORCES it and
 no authoritative range was stated in either plane before this:
   0 — registered. Sign-up plus a confirmed email address; nothing else is verified.
       No deposit address is issued and no withdrawal is accepted.
   1 — verified. Identity document, liveness, a face match against the document, and
       a passed sanctions/PEP screen. Deposits and withdrawals are permitted.
   2 — enhanced. Everything in 1 plus proof of address and source of funds. Carries
       raised transaction limits (the limits themselves are not modelled yet).
   3 — elevated. Enhanced due diligence; set only by a human reviewer, never
       automatically.
 Banking gates BOTH directions of money movement on >= 1. The value is set by an
 admin in the identity plane and mirrored onto the money plane by the one-way
 lifecycle bridge; banking never authors it.

role_is_break_glass.title: role_is_break_glass
role_is_break_glass.description:
True when `role` above came from concierge's OWNER_SUBJECTS emergency allowlist
 rather than from `users.role`. Carried here only for wire parity — the money plane
 has no allowlist of its own and never sets it.

suspended_by.title: suspended_by
suspended_by.description:
WHY the account is disabled, and therefore who may undo it — concierge splits the
 old blocking verb into a lapsing `admin_hold` and a ratified `governance` verdict,
 and an empty string is a THIRD case: an account suspended before the field existed,
 which keeps the one-act, never-lapsing semantics it was actually suspended under.

 Carried here only for wire parity, like `role_is_break_glass` above: the money plane
 learns of a freeze through the one-way lifecycle bridge's SUSPENDED/REINSTATED
 events, never by reading this, and never sets it. Absent them the parity round trip
 in `cabinet/backend/tests/concierge_parity.rs` re-encodes short and fails, which is
 exactly the drift that test exists to catch.

hold_expires_at.title: hold_expires_at
hold_expires_at.description: Unix SECONDS an "admin_hold" lapses; 0 when nothing lapses. Parity only, as above.

username.title: username
username.description: Parity with concierge.v1.UserProfile.username, like the two above.

user_id.title: user_id
user_id.description: The hub's canonical user id (a UUID) — this is the JWT `sub`, never Google's sub.

role.title: role
role.description:
Kept wire-identical with concierge.v1.UserSummary (the cabinet TS is aliased to the
 concierge shape). The money plane doesn't serve the role here — the cabinet reads it
 from concierge's login summary — so this stays empty; the field exists for parity.

role_is_break_glass.title: role_is_break_glass
role_is_break_glass.description:
Parity with concierge.v1.UserSummary.role_is_break_glass — the money plane does not
 serve it, but the field number must not be reused.

banking.v1.UserSummary.title: UserSummary
banking.v1.UserSummary.description:
Minimal principal snapshot returned with a freshly issued token pair, so the BFF
 can populate a session without a second round trip.

aum.title: aum
aum.description: The fund's total AUM to mark it at — decimal USDT string, as everywhere on this wire.

banking.v1.ValuationOverrideTerms.title: ValuationOverrideTerms
banking.v1.ValuationOverrideTerms.description:
The immutable subject of a VALUATION-OVERRIDE consilium — a NAV mark the move guard
 refuses (banking#232). The direct `PostFundValuation` caps a move at `MAX_NAV_MOVE_PCT`
 against the previous mark AND the mark anchoring a rolling window, and carries no flag
 to lift it; a genuine re-mark past the cap is put to the owners instead. Executing the
 consilium derives NAV from the LIVE unit supply at that moment and records the mark with
 the initiator as `posted_by`, so the redeem cooldown binds them exactly as a direct post
 would.

deposit_addresses.title: deposit_addresses
deposit_addresses.description: a rail to top up on (per network)

amount.title: amount
amount.description: gross debited from the user (decimal USDT)

net_amount.title: net_amount
net_amount.description: amount − fee, the amount sent on-chain

banking.v1.Withdrawal.title: Withdrawal
banking.v1.Withdrawal.description:
A user withdrawal aggregate, projected. `state` advances queued → processing →
 completed (settled on confirmations) | failed (voided, refunded); a queued one may
 also be cancelled (voided, refunded).

amount.title: amount
amount.description: gross decimal USDT debited from the source

source.title: source
source.description: user | treasury — which account funds it (`treasury`: an approved payment out of banking's treasury, D17)

banking.v1.WithdrawalQueueItem.title: WithdrawalQueueItem
banking.v1.WithdrawalQueueItem.description:
One withdrawal awaiting operator action. `email` is the mirrored identity email
 (may be empty if the bridge hasn't populated it); `created_at` is unix seconds.

created_at.title: created_at
created_at.description: Unix SECONDS the user was provisioned (joined).

role_is_break_glass.title: role_is_break_glass
role_is_break_glass.description:
True when `role` above came from the OWNER_SUBJECTS emergency allowlist rather than
 from `users.role` — see UserProfile.role_is_break_glass. This is the field that
 stops the console listing an "owner" the consilium has never heard of.

suspended_by.title: suspended_by
suspended_by.description:
Why the account is disabled; see UserProfile.suspended_by. On the list because a
 held account and a suspended one need different action buttons, and a console that
 cannot tell them apart offers the wrong one.

hold_expires_at.title: hold_expires_at
hold_expires_at.description: Unix SECONDS an "admin_hold" lapses. 0 when nothing lapses.

username.title: username
username.description: See UserProfile.username. ListUsers' query matches it as it matches the email.

concierge.v1.AdminUserSummary.title: AdminUserSummary
concierge.v1.AdminUserSummary.description:
A lightweight user row for the operator console's user list (not the full profile).
 Named distinctly from auth.proto's login `UserSummary` (same package).

concierge.v1.AdmissionVote.title: AdmissionVote
concierge.v1.AdmissionVote.description:
Deliberately its own enum rather than a reuse of RemovalVote: "remove/keep" and
 "admit/reject" are different questions, and a surface that renders the wrong verb on
 a governance vote is a surface that gets a vote cast by mistake.

delegates.title: delegates
delegates.description: Aliases of this catalog its holders may grant and revoke (GrantPermission).

user_id.title: user_id
user_id.description: The concierge user id — the access token's `sub`.

concierge.v1.ClientTokenResponse.title: ClientTokenResponse
concierge.v1.ClientTokenResponse.description:
A relying party's token pair. Expiries are unix SECONDS. Deliberately carries no
 profile: the client reads that from `UserDirectory.GetMe` with the access token, and
 GetMe is also what it re-checks `permissions` against on every request.

reason.title: reason
reason.description: Required; recorded as the void reason. At most 200 characters.

code.title: code
code.description: The `code` query parameter the browser brought back to the redirect_uri.

redirect_uri.title: redirect_uri
redirect_uri.description: The redirect_uri sent to authorize, byte for byte.

code_verifier.title: code_verifier
code_verifier.description: The PKCE verifier whose S256 challenge was sent to authorize.

fund.title: fund
fund.description: The fund whose terms change, in words a person recognises (not a service id).

current.title: current
current.description:
The terms in force today. Absent when the fund charges nothing yet — a product with
 no policy charges no fee, so "none" is a real current state, not a missing field.

reason.title: reason
reason.description: Why, in the operator's words. Required, and rendered attributed to them.

approval_url.title: approval_url
approval_url.description: Absolute URL of the approval page, carrying the opaque token.

code.title: code
code.description:
The secret code the owner types on that page. Held only until the mail is sent,
 then cleared from the delivery row.

concierge.v1.FeePolicyApprovalMail.title: FeePolicyApprovalMail
concierge.v1.FeePolicyApprovalMail.description:
An owner asked to approve new fee terms for a fund.

 Shaped like PaymentApprovalMail — a seated owner, a verified address, the operator's
 reason set apart as theirs, a link on our origin and the code that arms it — and it
 describes what an owner must actually be able to check: the terms in force NOW beside
 the terms PROPOSED, field by field. A fee change is a change to the price of every
 investor in the fund, and an approval mail that showed only the new number would have
 the owner approve a difference they cannot see.

subject_user_id.title: subject_user_id
subject_user_id.description:
Concierge canonical id of the investor. MUST equal the request's user_id; the relay
 refuses the mail otherwise.

fund.title: fund
fund.description: The fund whose terms change, in words a person recognises.

current.title: current
current.description: The terms in force until `effective_at`. Absent when the fund charged nothing.

proposed.title: proposed
proposed.description: The terms that apply from `effective_at`. Required.

effective_at.title: effective_at
effective_at.description: Unix seconds the new terms take effect.

link.title: link
link.description:
Cabinet-relative path of the page showing the full terms, e.g. `/funds/qn/fees`.
 Must start with a single `/`; empty means the cabinet's front page.

concierge.v1.FeePolicyNoticeMail.title: FeePolicyNoticeMail
concierge.v1.FeePolicyNoticeMail.description:
One investor told that the fee terms of a fund they hold are changing.

 `subject_user_id` exists beside SendGovernanceMailRequest.user_id for the reason
 PaymentConsentMail gives: no seat is involved, so the only fact this plane can hold
 the money plane to is that the person it is writing to IS the person the notice is
 about. A caller that fans one investor's notice out to a second mailbox has to
 contradict itself in the same message to do it.

 No code and no decision: the terms were set — by the operator within the house terms,
 or by the owners' consilium beyond them — and this is the investor being told before
 they take effect, with the same notice either way. `link` is a CABINET-RELATIVE path —
 the money plane names no host at all; this plane hangs it off its own cabinet origin.

management_bps.title: management_bps
management_bps.description: Annual management fee, in basis points of `basis`.

performance_bps.title: performance_bps
performance_bps.description: Performance fee over the high-water mark, in basis points of the gain.

hurdle_bps.title: hurdle_bps
hurdle_bps.description: Annual hurdle the gain must clear before the performance fee is due. 0 = none.

basis.title: basis
basis.description: invested_capital | market_value — what the management fee is charged on.

crystallization.title: crystallization
crystallization.description:
monthly | quarterly | semi_annual | annual — how often the performance fee
 crystallizes.

concierge.v1.FeeTerms.title: FeeTerms
concierge.v1.FeeTerms.description:
One set of fee terms, as the money plane's `FeePolicy` spells them: basis points and
 two closed vocabularies. Rendered HERE as percentages and words — the money plane
 never hands this plane a pre-rendered "2.5%", because a string it renders is a string
 it can make say anything. Every `_bps` is refused above 10 000 (100%), and `basis` and
 `crystallization` are refused outside their closed sets: an unknown word means the two
 planes disagree about what the terms ARE, which is a rejected call, not a line of mail.

concierge.v1.GovernanceMailKind.title: GovernanceMailKind
concierge.v1.GovernanceMailKind.description: The typed governance mails this plane knows how to render.

revision.title: revision
revision.description: Monotonic across the whole governance surface. Refetch when it moves.

at.title: at
at.description:
Unix seconds the tick was produced, so a client can tell a live stream from a
 wedged one.

heartbeat.title: heartbeat
heartbeat.description: True for the periodic keepalive, which carries the current revision unchanged.

username.title: username
username.description: The holder's handle; empty when they have none. A delegate sees it as it sees the email.

reason.title: reason
reason.description: Recorded on the grant and the audit row.

account.title: account
account.description: An email or a username: one handle, resolved the way a password sign-in resolves it.

reason.title: reason
reason.description:
REQUIRED. A brake that stops someone's money with no stated cause cannot be
 reviewed afterwards, and the owners asked to ratify it are reading exactly this.

hold_expires_at.title: hold_expires_at

concierge.v1.PaymentApprovalMail.title: PaymentApprovalMail
concierge.v1.PaymentApprovalMail.description:
An owner asked to approve a payment of fund-owned money.

 WHY NOT PayoutApprovalMail. That template opens with "a request to pay fund revenue
 out on-chain" and labels its middle rows Network and Destination address. A payment
 is a transfer between two claims the platform holds — `Piggybank → Revenue`, or into a
 service's pooled funds, or off the platform — and rendering it through the payout
 copy would mail the whole roster a sentence naming the wrong claim and the wrong rail
 on a money move they are being asked to authorize. The one thing an approval mail
 must do is describe correctly what is being approved, so a payment gets its own.

 The recipient rule is the payout one: a seated owner, resolved from the identity
 record, and nobody else. Field rules are PaymentConsentMail's — every string is
 bounded in bytes and refused if it carries a control character, `tier` is a closed
 set, and `reason` is required and rendered attributed to the operator who typed it.

subject_user_id.title: subject_user_id
subject_user_id.description:
Concierge canonical id of the user whose money moves. MUST equal the request's
 user_id; the relay refuses the mail otherwise.

initiator_email.title: initiator_email
initiator_email.description: The operator who opened the payment. Shown so the subject knows who is asking.

tier.title: tier
tier.description:
internal | service | external. A closed set: an unknown tier is a bug in the money
 plane, not a string to render at a person deciding whether to part with money.

source.title: source
source.description: Where the money leaves from, in words a person recognises (not an account id).

destination.title: destination
destination.description: Where it lands, in words a person recognises.

reason.title: reason
reason.description:
Why the payment was opened, written by the operator and shown to the subject
 VERBATIM. Required — a consent request with no stated reason is one nobody can
 judge. Rendered under its own label so it never reads as a platform statement, and
 refused outright if it carries a control character: the text part of a mail is not
 escaped, so a newline here would forge the Amount/To lines this mail exists to show.

approval_url.title: approval_url
approval_url.description: Absolute URL of the consent page, carrying the opaque token.

code.title: code
code.description: The secret code the subject types on that page.

concierge.v1.PaymentConsentMail.title: PaymentConsentMail
concierge.v1.PaymentConsentMail.description:
One user's consent to a payment that moves their own money.

 WHY subject_user_id EXISTS BESIDE SendGovernanceMailRequest.user_id. Every other kind
 is addressed to a fund owner, and "is this recipient an owner?" is a fact this plane
 holds independently of anything the money plane says. This kind has no such fact to
 check against: any user may consent to their own transfer, so "is this the right
 recipient?" is unanswerable from the addressing field alone. So the money plane must
 state, in the TYPED payload, whose money is moving — and the relay refuses unless the
 user it is being asked to write to IS that person. A caller that fans one consent out
 to a second mailbox has to contradict itself in the same message to do it.

 It is a redundancy on purpose. The address is still resolved HERE from the identity
 record and never taken from either field.

subject_user_id.title: subject_user_id
subject_user_id.description: Concierge canonical id of the user whose money the payment would have moved.

outcome.title: outcome
outcome.description:
TOKEN_BURNED (five wrong codes on the consent page) or INVALIDATED (the consent was
 voided under the subject — sessions revoked, email changed). A closed set.

reason.title: reason
reason.description:
Why the consent died, as a closed word this plane turns into its own phrase:
 WRONG_CODES (the only reason for TOKEN_BURNED), SESSIONS_REVOKED or EMAIL_CHANGED (the
 two reasons for INVALIDATED). Any other word, or a pair that does not match, is refused.

tier.title: tier
tier.description: internal | service | external — the consent kind's closed set.

source.title: source
source.description: Where the money would have left from, in words a person recognises.

destination.title: destination
destination.description: Where it would have landed, in words a person recognises.

amount.title: amount
amount.description:
The amount, spelled by the money plane (`1 200.00 USDT`): digits with the usual
 separators, one ASCII space, an upper-case currency code. Repeated in the subject line
 and in the subject's inbox, so anything else is refused.

payment_id.title: payment_id
payment_id.description: The payment's id, a UUID. Shown to staff so they can find the order; not to the subject.

concierge.v1.PaymentOutcomeMail.title: PaymentOutcomeMail
concierge.v1.PaymentOutcomeMail.description:
A payment cancelled because its subject's consent could no longer be given.

 WHY NOT PayoutOutcomeMail. That one is the consilium's record and goes to seated owners
 only; the people this one is FOR are the payment's subject — whose consent link was
 attacked, or whose sessions were just revoked — and the staff member who opened the
 order, who is usually an admin. Neither holds a seat.

 `subject_user_id` exists for the reason PaymentConsentMail gives, with one widening: the
 relay accepts the request's user_id when it IS that subject, or when it names an admin or
 an owner. Which of the two it was decides the copy (the subject is told what to do about
 their mailbox; staff get the order's details) and whether an inbox trace is written (the
 subject only).

 Nothing here is a secret and nothing can be a link: no URL, no code. Why the consent
 died is a closed word the platform phrases itself, and the amount must read as money —
 no money-plane text reaches a sentence of ours.

approval_url.title: approval_url
approval_url.description: Absolute URL of the approval page, carrying the opaque token.

code.title: code
code.description:
The secret code the owner types on that page. Held only until the mail is sent,
 then cleared from the delivery row.

outcome.title: outcome
outcome.description:
APPROVED / REJECTED / EXPIRED / CANCELLED / EXECUTED / EXECUTION_FAILED, or
 TOKEN_BURNED under the burn kind.

network.title: network
network.description: The payout pair. Empty for a payment.

tier.title: tier
tier.description:
The payment tuple. Empty for a payout. Same rules as PaymentApprovalMail: `tier`
 is the closed set, `source` and `destination` are words a person recognises, and
 `reason` is the operator's own text, shown attributed and refused if it carries a
 control character.

fund.title: fund
fund.description:
The fee terms description. Empty for a payout and for a payment. Same rules as
 FeePolicyApprovalMail: `fund` is words a person recognises and may not carry a
 link, `current` is absent when the fund charged nothing (a real state, not a
 missing field), `proposed` is required, and `reason` — the operator's words, shown
 attributed — is empty under the burn kind.

mark.title: mark
mark.description:
The NAV mark description: `fund` as above, and the value the consilium was asked to
 mark it at, spelled by the money plane as an amount is (`5 000.00 USDT`). Empty for
 the other three. A mark used to ride the payment tuple (`Amount: 5000`, `To: AUM
 5000 USDT`, `Type: service`), which told the owners money had moved when a mark
 moves none; with this field filled the relay renders it as the value it is. Same
 rules as an amount: one line, and it may not carry a link.

concierge.v1.PayoutOutcomeMail.title: PayoutOutcomeMail
concierge.v1.PayoutOutcomeMail.description:
How a consilium ended — over a revenue payout, over a payment, over a fund's fee
 terms, or over a fund's NAV mark — and, under APPROVAL_TOKEN_BURNED, that one of its
 tokens burned.

 ONE message for four subjects, additively. The burn notice already rides this shape
 under its own kind, so a payment consilium's outcome and burn ride it too, and so do a
 fee-policy consilium's and a valuation override's, rather than each growing a message
 of their own: `network` + `address` describe a payout, `source` + `destination`
 (+ `tier`, `reason`) describe a payment, `fund` + `proposed` (+ `current`, `reason`)
 describe fee terms, `fund` + `mark` (+ `reason`) describe a NAV mark, and the renderer
 switches on which description is filled. A caller fills exactly one and leaves the
 others empty.

Deliberately NEUTRAL verbs, where the owner consilia use remove/keep and

 something read against UserProposal.kind — and a vocabulary that is correct only when
 cross-referenced is one that eventually gets rendered wrong. The kind-specific verb
 belongs on the SURFACE, which knows the kind; this is which way the voter pushed.

Recorded verbatim on the audit row. Optional here: revoking sessions is the

user_id.description:
Concierge canonical user id of the recipient. The address is resolved HERE, from
 the identity record, so the money plane cannot redirect a governance mail.

dedupe_key.title: dedupe_key
dedupe_key.description:
Idempotency key. The same key never sends twice.

 A key names ONE mail: one kind, to one recipient. Reusing a key for the same mail is a
 retry and answers `enqueued: false`; reusing it for a different recipient or kind is
 refused ALREADY_EXISTS, because the key is unique across the whole queue. So a kind
 told to several people — PAYMENT_OUTCOME to the subject and to each staff member —
 needs a key per copy.

The user's platform access role (snake_case: investor/operator/admin/owner).

role_is_break_glass.description:
True when `role` above came from the OWNER_SUBJECTS emergency allowlist rather than
 from `users.role`. See UserSummary.role_is_break_glass in auth.proto — same flag,
 same meaning: real authority, granted by the environment while the fund has no

suspended_by.title: suspended_by
suspended_by.description:
WHY the account is disabled — and therefore who may undo it. Empty on an active
 user, and also on one suspended before this field existed (those keep the old
 one-act, never-lapsing semantics they were actually suspended under).
   "admin_hold"  — one operator's brake; lapses at hold_expires_at; ReinstateUser
                   lifts it in one act.
   "governance"  — the owners' ratified verdict; never lapses; ReinstateUser
                   refuses and names ProposeUserReinstatement.

hold_expires_at.title: hold_expires_at
hold_expires_at.description: Unix SECONDS an "admin_hold" lapses. 0 when nothing lapses.

permissions.title: permissions
permissions.description:
What the caller may do, concrete: no alias, no wildcard. Filled by GetMe only. To a
 relying party, its tenant's namespace and nothing else; to a first-party session, the
 seat's permissions plus every tenant's. A relying party gates on this alone.

username.title: username
username.description:
A handle beside the email, interchangeable with it wherever an account is named.
 Empty when the account has none.

subject_user_id.title: subject_user_id
subject_user_id.description:
Any user — NOT necessarily an owner. That is the difference from OwnerAdmission,
 and the reason none of its roster checks have an analogue here.

reason.title: reason
reason.description: Why, in the initiator's words. Required, and shown to every voter.

peers.title: peers
peers.description:
Every owner except the initiator, with their answers. Never empty: a proposal with
 nobody to agree is refused at open rather than left open and unpassable.

owner_count.title: owner_count
owner_count.description: Owners at open. The initiator is counted but does not vote.

threshold.title: threshold
threshold.description:
How many of `peers` must vote FOR, frozen at open — so a surface shows the bar this
 proposal is actually measured against, not one re-derived from a roster that moved.

concierge.v1.UserProposal.title: UserProposal
concierge.v1.UserProposal.description:
The owners' verdict over one PERSON's standing.

 It passes on a MAJORITY of the snapshotted voters, not the unanimity the OWNER
 consilia demand, and the difference is deliberate. Unanimity guards the owner roster
 because a minority able to add owners by majority grows itself into a majority.
 Neither thing decided here has that property: `admin` cannot vote in any consilium
 and cannot be granted `owner`, and a suspension is defensive and reversible by the
 same body. Against that, unanimity here would COST safety — a hold lapses in 24h, so
 ratifying one races a clock, and under unanimity one unreachable owner does not delay
 the verdict, they decide it by releasing a compromised account at the deadline.

 What is preserved is the property that matters: the initiator is excluded from the
 voter set and the threshold is at least one, so no single actor ever acts alone.

concierge.v1.UserProposalKind.title: UserProposalKind
concierge.v1.UserProposalKind.description:
What a UserProposal decides. Three kinds share one message because all three are the
 same question — "do the owners agree to change this person's standing?" — differing
 only in what the verdict writes.

concierge.v1.UserProposalState.title: UserProposalState
concierge.v1.UserProposalState.description:
The six states, again as their own enum: proto enum VALUES share one namespace per
 package, so the identical states have to be spelled three times even though the
 domain models them with one type.

user_id.title: user_id
user_id.description: The concierge canonical user id (a UUID) — this is the JWT `sub`, never Google's sub.

role.title: role
role.description:
The user's platform access role (snake_case: investor/operator/admin/owner), so the
 BFF can gate the admin console at sign-in without a second round trip. Read-only.

role_is_break_glass.title: role_is_break_glass
role_is_break_glass.description:
True when `role` above came from the OWNER_SUBJECTS emergency allowlist rather than
 from `users.role`. It is real authority, but it is the environment's and not the
 register's: it disappears the moment the fund has its first persisted owner, and it
 seats nobody. A client MUST render it as a warning, never as ownership.

username.title: username
username.description: Empty when the account has no handle.

concierge.v1.UserSummary.title: UserSummary
concierge.v1.UserSummary.description:
Minimal principal snapshot returned with a freshly issued token pair, so the BFF
 can populate a session without a second round trip.

connect-protocol-version.description: Define the version of the Connect protocol
